...after they relate to their end?
Solution. Go to the example of the aforesaid rubric. The hermit asked of the will, why it is often confused in choice? Solution in the same place. Will, said the hermit, do you have rest in loving and in hating? Solution. No rest can be from contrary ends. And go to the example of virtue. Freedom, said the hermit, how can you be in servitude, being what you are, without any deprivation of your conditions? Solution in the same place.

*Of Exemplary Questions of the Branches of the Vegetal Tree.*

How does one man take a way in deceiving another man? Solution. Go to the example of the aforesaid rubric. How does one man know how to guard himself from deception, which another man wishes to do to him? Solution in the same place. Why are men who expect to arrange their will and make satisfaction for their transgressions, when they are for the most part infirm, deceived? Solution in the same place. Why should men imagine, recall, and love temperance at the beginning of a meal? Solution in the same place.

*Of Exemplary Questions of the Branches of the Sensual Tree.*

The hermit asked of Nature, why it was stronger than custom? Solution. Go to the example of the branch of the sensual tree. How does great contrariety conquer and destroy small concord? Solution. Go to the example of the branches of the sensual tree. Why should new honor avoid the company of old honor? Solution in the same place. Why should a rich man avoid the company of a poor man? Solution in the same place.

*Of Exemplary Questions of the Branches of the Imaginal Tree.*

It was asked of imagination, who conquered it? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. It was asked of discretion, who conquered it? Solution in the same place. It was asked of a man who is in mortal sin, whether he ought to use the goods he possesses? Solution in the same place. It was asked of indiscretion, in what is it greater? Solution. No indiscretion is greater than that by which a man has confidence in his mortal enemy. And go to the example of virtue.

*Of Questions of the Branches of the Human and Corporal Tree.*

It was asked of art, whether it was greater than law? Solution. Go to the example of the aforesaid rubric. The King asked Raymond, how he would recognize a good messenger whom he wished to send to a certain Prince? Solution in the same place. It was asked of the King, how he recognized the enmity of a man? Solution in the same place. It was asked of the demon, how he deceived men? Solution in the same place.

**Questions of branches.** 531

The Philosopher asked of Martin's branch, since it itself is one branch, how are there many branches in it in potential? Solution. A mass of iron is one, in which were in potential the iron of a nail and the iron of a knife. The Philosopher asked of Martin's orchard branch, whether it is visible? Sol. The branch said that it was twofold, and that it was visible, insofar as it is the nature of an elemental branch, and it is invisible, insofar as it is vegetal. The Philosopher asked of Martin's orchard branch, whether its flowers participate more in nature with it according to the vegetal tree, or according to the elemental tree? Solution. All participation is greater by species than by genus.

**On the Questions of the branches of the sensual tree.**

Of what are the branches of the sensual tree? Solution. Go to the aforesaid heading. How are the branches of the sensual tree? Solution in the same place. What kind are the branches of the sensual tree? Solution in the same place. The Philosopher asked of the branches of Martin's horse, how are they situated? Solution in the same place. The Philosopher asked of the eyes of Martin's horse, how many are its branches? Solution. Go to the heading of virtue. The Philosopher asked, whether the visibility of an apple is closer to visivity than the visibility of a stone or a flame? Solution. All visivity participates more internally with vegetal visibility than with elemental visibility: but because the vegetative cannot be seen, nor its own simple individual, visivity itself participates more strongly with the visibility of a stone and a flame than with vegetal visibility. Therefore, stone and flame are more visible than an apple. The Philosopher asked of luxury, whether it participated as strongly with the heart as with the eyes? Solution. Luxury responded that it participated internally with the heart, and externally with the eyes. The Philosopher asked of visivity and audivity, whether they were different by reason of eyes and ears, or by themselves? Solution. If the difference of visivity and audivity were not proper, but appropriated, the sensitive power would not have natural commonality by itself. The Philosopher asked of the heart, why it has greater concordance with a pleasant odor than with a beautiful color? Solution. No color truly comes to the heart externally.

**On the Questions of the branches of the Imaginal tree.**

What kind are the imaginative branches? Solution. Go to the aforesaid heading. How many are the imaginative branches? Solution in the same place. Imagination, how does it imagine? Solution in the same place. The hermit asked of imagination, whether, when it imagines a flame of fire, it imagines equally the figure and the splendor? Solution. Because light is an instrument for seeing, and figure is a common accident for seeing and touching, the imaginative power imagines light more strongly in the beginning than figure: but because figure participates more with corporeal externality, the imaginative power imagines figure more strongly in its situation than light. Imagination, said the hermit, do you imagine equally in the imagination of an apple, generation and corruption? Solution. Since the reason of the end is the beginning, imagination imagines generation through the vegetative, and corruption through the elemental. Imaginative power, said the hermit, when you imagine a horse, what likeness

*On Questions of the branches of the*
*Imperial tree.*

What kind are the branches of the Imperial tree? Solution: Go to the aforementioned rubric. How many are the branches of the Imperial tree? Solution: Ibid. By what kind of branches are the branches of the Prince better signified? Solution: Ibid. The hermit asked the branches of the Prince whether they are general or special? Solution. The branches said that according to the office of the Prince they are general, and insofar as the Prince is one man, they are special.

*On Questions of the justice*
*of the Prince.*

"Prince," said the hermit, "do you love your special justice more than your general justice?" Solution. The Prince said that he is subject to public utility: therefore, he does not have the liberty, according to justice, to love a special good as much as a public good. "Prince, why are you a common person?" Solution. The Prince said that he was a common person so that justice might be among men. It was asked of the Prince whether he loved justice more than charity? Solution. The Prince replied that he loved justice more than charity insofar as he is a common person: and insofar as he is one man, he loved charity more than justice. "Prince, do you love your son more than your people?" Solution. Justice does not consent that a special good be loved more than a public good.

*On Questions of the love of the Prince.*

It was asked of the Prince, what kind of love his should be? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric in the branches of the imperial tree. It was asked of the Prince, how he reigned for so long? Solution: Ibid. It was asked of the Prince, why he made his people fear him more than love him? Solution. No proud man does anything out of love. It was asked of the Prince, why he had fear? Solution. The Prince said that he had fear because his people feared him more than they loved him.

*On Questions of the fear of the Prince.*

It was asked of the Prince, what kind of fear his should be, and what kind his people's? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric in the branches of the imperial tree. It was asked of the Prince whether he had greater fear of love than of death? Solution. A good Prince, out of love for his people, exposes himself to the danger of death in war. It was asked of love and fear, in what they had greater concordance? Solution. Love and fear replied that that question should be put to a good Prince and a good people. It was asked of the Prince whether he had greater fear of his people than of God? Solution. The Prince replied that from the fear of God follows liberty, and from the fear of his people follows servitude.

*On Questions of the wisdom of the Prince.*

What kind are the conditions of the Prince? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. By what condition is the Prince more to be feared? Solution: Ibid.

From the Prince it was asked, whether it was as necessary for him to love charity as wisdom? Solution. The Prince said that according to his office, wisdom was more necessary for him than charity, because wisdom has concordance with justice, and charity with money. From the Prince's wisdom it was asked, whether it had fear? Solution. The Prince's wisdom responded that according to its nature it did not have fear, nor according to the nature of justice and the sword, which are its friends.

*On the Questions of the Prince's power.*

From the Prince it was asked, why he desired to be powerful? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric in the branches of the imperial tree. From the Prince it was asked, whether he loved wisdom more than power? Solution. The Prince said that he reigned with the wisdom of his counsel. Power of the Prince, why do you weep? Solution. Power responded that it wept because the Prince kept it idle, and strongly vexed it in doing evil. From the Prince's power it was asked, whether it had fear? Solution. Power responded that it had fear of the liberty of its people, which was growing.

*On the Questions of the Prince's honor.*

From the Prince it was asked, from what was his honor? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric in the branches of the Imperial tree. Prince, why do you love honor more than money? Solution. The Prince said that he was more the image of God through honor than through money. Honor of the Prince, why do you weep? Solution. Honor said that it wept because the Prince kept it dishonored, inasmuch as he sought to honor himself more than God. Honor of the Prince, do you have fear? Solution. No honor can fall from such a height into weakness, as the honor of the Prince.

*On the Questions of the Prince's liberty.*

From the Prince it was asked, whether he knew what his liberty is? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric in the branches of the Imperial tree. Prince, why do you weep? Solution. The Prince said that he wept because his people loved him more out of fear than out of love. Prince, why do you have liberty? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue. From the Prince's liberty it was asked, how it came into servitude? Solution there.

*On the Questions of the branches of the Apostolic tree.*

What are the branches of the apostolic tree like? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. From the Church it was asked, why are its precepts [as they are]? Solution there. Church, why do you weep? Solution. The Church responded that it wept because all nations are not obedient to it. Feast, why do you weep? Solution. The feast responded that it wept because the Jews observed their Sabbaths better than Christians observed the Lord's days.

*De Quæstionibus foliorum arboris*
*humanalis.*

*De Quantitate.*

It was asked of the taste, whether it had one quantity or several? Solution.
taste or by sensing. From imagination it was asked, how it imagines the ternary number? Solution. Imagination responded, that it first imagined the quantity of one, and afterwards the quantity of a second, then the quantity of a third; from all these three particular quantities it drew one common quantity, existing under the ternary number. And go to the rubric of virtue. From imagination it was asked, whether the number which it produces has any real quantity, or if it is only from similarities? Solution. Imagination responded, that that number which it produces from substances, does not signify any real entity according to the nature of the substances from which it draws the number, but insofar as it sustains that number in itself, it is an act, which it has in the number as a real being in this, that it is its own act, which is of its own nature and virtue, and in this passage there is much of Philosophy.

*Of the Questions of the leaves of the human tree.*

*Of Quantity.*

It was asked of the quantity of man, how from many it is one? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Soul, said the hermit, since you do not have extensive quantity, how are you extended through the whole body of Martin? Solution. Just as in an apple the taste can be extended through the whole color, although taste is not of the species of color, so the rational soul can be extended through the whole body, although its quantity does not have the nature of length, breadth, and depth. Rational soul,

since your substance is not augmentable, and you are through the whole body of a great man, how can you be through its whole, when you were entirely in that body when it was small? Solution. Just as the taste of an apple is extended in the color, although it is not of the genus of color, so the rational soul is extended according to how the body is extended, although it is not of the nature of length, breadth, and depth. Rational soul, do you have quantity? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue.

*Of the Questions of the leaves of moral virtues.*

*Of Quantity.*

Justice, since you do not have real quantity, how can you grow or diminish? Solution. Imagination grows and diminishes the likeness of substance, although that likeness is not a real being, which it multiplies or diminishes, according to whether imagination has a great or small act. Justice, is your quantity visible? Solution. No morality can be visible, because it does not have color. Justice, do you grow in act through potency, or through an object? Solution. No passion multiplies itself. From justice it was asked, whether it had quantity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric.

*Of the Questions of the leaves of the vicious tree.*

*Of Quantity.*

Lust, do you have quantity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Lust, how do you grow or diminish, since you are a privation of chastity, and privation is not the subject of quanti-

of quantity, what is its habit? Solution: there. Lust, do you have any real quantity? Solution. Lust responded that it could not have any real quantity, since it was a pure privation of chastity. Lust, since no moral privation posits any real entity, whence is your quantity? Solution. Lust responded that it arose from an inordinate movement against order and matrimony. *Concerning the Questions of the leaves of the Imperial tree.*

*Concerning Quantity.*

How ought a Judge use quantity in judgment? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How can the knowledge of civil law be placed in other terms? Solution: there. How are buying and selling conditioned by quantity? Solution: there. With what will the Judge find the truth? Solution: there.

*Concerning the Questions of the leaves of the Apostolic tree.*

*Concerning Quantity.*

It is asked whether there is quantity in the Most Holy Trinity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since the divine persons are distinct, how can they be without quantity? Solution. In no hypostasis that is of the nature of infinity and eternity can there be quantity. Since the divine essence is in distinct persons, by what means is it indivisible? Solution. The Father is the whole essence, and from His whole self He produces the Son; therefore the whole essence remains in the Father and

[Column 2]

in the Son, and the same is true of the Holy Spirit. Since divine goodness is not created goodness, how can it be without quantity, it itself being terminated in created goodness? Solution. In an apple, taste is not of the nature of color, and it is delimited by distinction in color.

*Concerning the Questions of the leaves of the Celestial tree.*

*Concerning Quantity.*

How is quantity considered in the firmament? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How are discrete quantities considered in the sun? Solution: there. How does the quantity of fire receive influence from the quantity of the sun, which does not abandon its own subject? Solution: there. How do the discrete quantities of the firmament stand under one continuous quantity? Solution. In goodness, that which makes good, that which can be made good, and to make good, are distinct by discrete quantities, which are of the common quantity of goodness.

*Concerning the Questions of the leaves of the Angelic tree.*

*Concerning Quantity.*

It is asked, whether an Angel has quantity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since an Angel does not have the nature of a body, how are its discrete quantities joined together? Solution. The lover stands in the beloved through loving, and in the movement of a ship, sailors are moved. The discrete quantities of the Angel's substance multiply the common quantity situated in a circle, or in a triangle.

Whether there are more good Angels than bad, since there are more bad men than good? Solution. No magnitude of a bad Angel has concordance with the magnitude of God.

*Of the Questions of the leaves of the eternal tree.*

*Of Quantity.*

How does eternity have quantity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned leaves. Does Lucifer consider the number of years? Solution. In the flame of fire there is no night, nor in the Empyrean Heaven is there but one day. Why does a demon not have hope? Solution. If in hell eternity had a number of years, any damned person could have hope in God. Does one angel have as great a quantity as another? Solution. All meritorious works of angels are not equal.

*Of the Questions of the leaves of the maternal tree.*

*Of Quantity.*

What is the greater maternity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned leaves. Is the moral quantity of Our Lady as great as the natural? Solution. The natural quantity of Christ's humanity is not of the moral quantity of Our Lady. Is the piety of Our Lady greater than the sin of a sinner? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue. Does Our Lady consider the number of saved and damned men? Solution. Every day Our Lady asks her Son that He make her the mother of more men.

*Of the Questions of the leaves of the tree of Jesus Christ.*

*Of Quantity.*

Since divine nature is infinite, how can it participate with quantity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned leaves. Since the humanity of Christ has a finite quantity, how can the whole person, who is God, be clothed from it, which person is indeed infinite? Solution. The divine will, which is a person, wills that the whole Son be incarnate: and the power of God can perfect all that the will, which is infinite, wills. How does the divine nature of Jesus Christ, which is a person, exist without quantity, and that the Son is incarnate, and not the Father, nor the Holy Spirit? Solution. The heat of pepper, and the heat of flame, insofar as it is heat, is not divisible. Since the Son is incarnate, and not the Father, nor the Holy Spirit, do only the Father and the Holy Spirit participate with human nature, like the Son? Solution. In an essence in which there is no quantity, there cannot be a comparison of greater and lesser.

**Questions on the leaves. 551**

**On Questions of the quality of the sensual tree.**

The heat which man feels, from what is it: Solution. Simple heat is from fire, and composite heat is from air and from earth, and it is from the sensitive faculty through sensing: just as a hammer, which belongs to a nail, and is the same through vegetating. And go to the leaves of the sensual tree. How does taste give pleasure through eating, and sight through seeing? Solution. Ibid. The sweetness which man feels in an apple, how is it led from potency to act? Solution. Ibid. From what does sensing live? Solution. Ibid.

**On Questions of the quality of the imaginal tree.**

How does imagination receive the likeness of real quality? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Since the moral goodness of Martin is not sensible, how can imagination itself imagine it: Solution. From the order of visible substances, imagination draws a likeness in the abstract. The words which the King spoke, does the intellect or the imaginative power receive them? Solution. Imagination is an instrument which stands in the middle of intellect and sense in the words which the King spoke. The words which memory recalls, does it imagine them? Solution. Thus imagination is an instrument of remembering, just as it is of understanding and loving.

**On Questions of the quality of the human tree.**

The qualities of man, how are they mutually situated? Solution. Go

to the aforesaid rubric. Is the heat of man a quality of him or of fire? Solution. The heat of air is a quality appropriated to the air itself, and it is a proper quality of fire. Is the sadness of man a proper quality of the body or of the soul? Solution. One quality is that which gives a corporeal passion, and another is that which gives a spiritual passion. Is the moral goodness of Martin a corporeal quality? Solution. Properly, justice is a quality of the soul acquired and appropriated to the body.

**On Questions of the quality of the virtues of the moral tree.**

How is the moral virtue of Martin determined by quality? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Is the prudence of Martin of one quality or of several? Solution. In one understanding, several likenesses are gathered and joined together. And go to the aforesaid rubric. Is one morality the quality of another? Solution. In pepper, passively, there are dryness, humidity, and coldness from heat, and in a lamp, the heat of oil is from the heat of the flame. How does moral quality grow? Solution. From a multitude of wood, the flame grows, which burns the wood.

**On Questions of the quality of the vices of the moral tree.**

Avarice, how are you evil? Solution. Avarice responds that it is evil because through malice it is a quality, just as magnitude is a quality good through goodness. And go to the aforesaid rubric. How does evil quality multiply? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Vicious quality, when

--- Page 566 ---
552      Questions of the Leaves.

Avarice, are you a quality in Martin, of whom you are a habit? Solution. If avarice were a quality by itself in Martin, whose habit it is, it would not incur guilt by itself.

*Concerning Questions of the quality of the imperial tree.*

A merchant promises to give good gold, and does not give good [gold], and a soldier promises to sell a good horse, and does not sell a good [one], therefore it is a question, whether the sale is valid or not? Solution. Justice does not wish that any stability stand by private promises. A soldier promises to sell a good horse, and sells a good [one], and a merchant promises to give good gold, and does not give good [gold], it is asked, whether the sale is valid, or not? Solution. No substance can exist without all those parts which are necessary to it. A merchant tests the horse, and it is not good, which the soldier says is good, and the merchant does not recognize the horse's defect, and believes that it is good, and pays the gold, and on the morrow he recognizes that the horse is not good: it is asked whether the sale is valid, or not? Solution. Justice, according to the Emperor, wills that the merchant use prudence, and if he does not wish to use it, that he be punished. But the Pope wills that the soldier use conscience, and if he does not wish to use it, God's justice wills that he be punished in the other world, or that he do penance in this world. Someone makes a will, in which he says that his wife, who is pregnant: if she has two sons, that the one who is born first should be the heir of his money. Finally his wife has two sons, and she does not know which of them was born first, it is asked, how the will of the testator will be fulfilled? Solution. When the conjoined antecedent is unknown due to ignorance, and in equality of paternity, the monies are equally divisible.

*Concerning Questions of the quality of the Apostolic tree. Concerning Baptism.*

Why is Baptism? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. How does Baptism cleanse man from sin? Solution. Ibid. A child who does not have understanding, and who does not consent to Baptism, how is he cleansed by the sacrament? Solution. In a child there are five trees, four receive the impression of the Sacrament; But the fifth receives the impression of the Sacrament in potential: like an apple in which the power of generating another apple is received, which comes into act through the Sacrament of Confirmation. If a child dies before he comes to the Sacrament of Confirmation, does that Sacrament benefit him at all? Solution. The impressions of the other trees cleanse those who bore the guilt of original sin, and grace is given to the fifth tree through the concordance of the others: without which grace, God's justice would do injury to the first trees, which received the character of the Sacrament.

*Concerning Questions of Confirmation.*

Why is Confirmation? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. If a child does not wish to consent to Confirmation, or does the Sacrament of Baptism benefit him at all? Solution. In the destruction of the form, the matter is destroyed. Do children who die before they are confirmed go to Purgatory? Solution. The soul of a baptized child who is not confirmed receives the character of the Sacrament in potential, who does not have guilt:

--- Page 567 ---
Quæstiones foliorum. 553

[Left Column]
...does not have: if in this age he has not used reason, because he did not have the instrument with which he could use it. If a man is not confirmed, and believes that he is confirmed, and dies before he is confirmed, is he cleansed from original sin? Solution. Good intention consumes guilt and sin.

**On Questions of Marriage.**

What is marriage? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is marriage? Solution there. How is marriage? Solution there. Martin consents to marriage, and his wife does not consent internally, but externally through words, I ask whether the marriage is valid? Solution. There are two laws, one is internal, and the other external; according to external law, the woman, Martin's wife, is bound, who, against that which was internal, moved her assent; the other internal law remains free, and if she consents afterwards, it is captured. And go to the rubric of virtue.

**On Questions of the Eucharist.**

Why is the Sacrament of the Altar? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. For what does the Sacrament of the Altar profit? Solution. No utility is greater than this, than to use its goodness with God. And go to the rubric of virtue. Since Christ is in heaven, how can he be at one time on multiple altars, and how can his body be in the host, which is so small, and since the matter of bread is transubstantiated into his body, why does Christ's body not grow? And why do the senses not perceive it in the Sacrament, namely by seeing, tasting, smelling, and touch-

[Right Column]
-ing? Solution there. What is the greater and nobler work that God and man can do in this world? Solution. The greater and nobler work consists in the greater participation of God and man. And go to the rubric of virtue.

**On Questions of Order.**

Why is Order? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why can no man make the Sacrament of the Altar, unless he is a priest? Solution. No nobler end stands without an ordered beginning and an ordered means. Why can a priest who is excommunicated confect the Sacrament of the Altar? Solution. The letters that are in the wax are not of the essence of the seal, nor of the essence of the man who puts those letters in the wax with the seal, but only the letters that are in the wax are impressions of the letters of the seal, whether the man is good or bad. In whom does a greater sin lie? Solution. In that man, in whom there can be greater virtue, there can be greater sin.

**On Questions of Penance.**

What is penance? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is penance? Solution there. Why is confession? Solution. Confession is, so that penance can be: because without confession, the priest would not know how to give penance, nor have thought of satisfaction. Why can a priest remit guilt to a man who confesses to him, and cannot remit it to himself? Solution. The keys of blessed Peter are common to all men, therefore it is necessary for every priest to be under the judgment of another.

*On Questions of the quality of the eternal tree.*

How is the moral quality of blessed Peter, which is terminated in a certain quantity, eternal? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Why is the punishment of Muhammad eternal, since it is the case that his sin is finite and terminated? Solution in the same place. Is the moral quality of blessed Peter multiplicable? Solution. The tail of eternity does not sustain that there is any multiplication in it. Why does Lucifer not have the freedom to do good? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue.

*On Questions of the quality of the maternal tree.*

How great are the moral qualities of Our Lady? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Why does a sinner have guilt, when he has despair, because his sin is great? Solution in the same place. Can Our Lady deny anything to a sinner who asks her with contrition and love? Solution in the same place. Since sins are so many and so great, and virtues are few in men, and God is just, how can He sustain so many evil men in the world? Solution. Naturally, every mother has pity for the passion of her Son.

*On Questions of the quality of the tree of Jesus Christ.*

Can God acquire moral virtues? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Why did Jesus Christ promise to be sold, bound, scourged, and Crucified? Solution in the same place. Je-

[Right Column]

-sus Christ, why did he not have a woman and boys or sons? Solution in the same place. Why was Jesus Christ poor? Solution in the same place.

*On Questions of the quality of the Divine tree.*

Why are the qualities of God not accidental? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. God loves Martin when he is good, and does not love him when he is bad, why is His love not accidental? Solution. If wax were a tile, fire would dry it out just as well as it dries out glass and coal. Since God is good by goodness, and great by greatness, how can He be His own goodness? Solution. If God were not His own goodness, the infinite magnitude of nature would not suffice for nature nor for goodness, and it would be finite: and the same is true of His infinite power, and this would be evil and vicious. The Father generates the Son, and because the Father and the Son are distinct persons, and the Father generates the Son from His goodness, why are the goodness of the Father and the Son not two goodnesses: and the same is true of other reasons? Solution. Reasons and nature are one and the same in number, so that nature is not good and great accidentally: and because the Father generates the Son from His nature, and from His goodness, infinity, and eternity, the Father is one, and the Son is another by generation, and the goodness and nature of both are one by infinity and eternity.

*Concerning questions of the relation of the imaginal tree.*

How does imagination receive
relation? Solutio. Go to the aforesaid
rubric. With which sense does
imagination have greater concordance
with relation? Solutio. No relation
is so imaginatively palpable: as the
relation of father and son, which is accepted
by seeing. Does imagination have some
entity of relation? Solutio. No
form is without action, nor any
matter without passion. Can imagination
draw relation from color? Solutio.
In a great intensity of the whiteness of a white

*Concerning questions of the relation of the human tree.*

What kind of relation is it that
is most natural in man? Solutio.
No relation is so natural to man
as that by which he himself is
definable, namely the relation of the benefactive,
the capable of being benefited, and to benefit. Why
is man more definable by relation
than by any other accident? Solutio.
No accident takes necessary parts in a
substance so strongly as relation does. In re-

lation of bonification does the relation
of the soul and body consist? Solutio. Go
to the aforesaid rubric. Does relation
consist in the rational soul? Solutio, in the same

*Concerning Questions of the relation of the
virtues of the moral tree.*

How does relation consist in
moral virtue? Solutio. Go to the
aforesaid rubric. Does relation consist
in the habit of virtue, when man uses
virtue? Solutio. In the habit of virtue, the
action of relation is in potentiality, and when
man uses virtue, the form has
its object in act. And go to the
rubric of virtue. Does relation in moral
virtue have some entity? Solutio.
Without some entity, no similitude
can exist. Is there a relation
between one virtue and another? Solutio.
Without the concordance of virtues, no
virtue could be against vice.

*Concerning questions of the relation of the vices
of the moral tree.*

How does relation consist in a
vicious habit? Solutio. Go to the
aforesaid rubric. How does the relation of vice
begin? Solutio, in the same place. Between
gluttony and lust, how is the relation
situated? Solutio. Through the abundance
of the elemental, vegetal, sensual,
and imaginal tree, the rational soul is
tempted by gluttony and lust, which
temptation indeed the situating of gluttony and
lust causes by forgetting chastity and temperance.
Since anger is a sudden movement, can
relation have any situating in it? Solutio. No
anger is without sadness and the passion of the agent.

558      Questions of the leaves.

*On Questions of the relation of the Imperial tree.*

**I**nstrument that is made concerning buying and selling, how ought it to be conditioned? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Why is a servant not admitted as testimony for his Lord? Solution. The relation of Lord and servitude is not a cause for equal judgment. The judge saw Martin kill Peter, before which judge Martin is not accused, but William is accused and punished by the judge, why does the judge punish William, and not Martin? Solution. In judgment, the judge is not (guided) by the relation of his eyes, but by the relation of his ears. How could the science of civil law be applied under brief principles, and general ones through those judgments? Solution. Go to the leaves of the imperial tree, and have knowledge of natural substances through this book, and the same is true for the accidents of natural and moral substances, and inquire through those according to the doctrine which we give in solving questions by relations, and by other accidents.

*On Questions of the relation of the Apostolic tree.*

**I**n the Most High Trinity, how is there a substantial relation without any accident? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Is the relation of the divine persons concerning properties, or is it concerning essence? Solution. In the divine will there is a common relation, just as will is common by essence, and in the lover, the beloved, and the act of loving, so is the relation sustained in personal properties, like will: and eternity requires this, so that the relation is not accidental. Could there be a relation between the Father and the Son without the Holy Spirit? Solution. No relation can be perfect without a singular and common property. The Holy Spirit loves the Father, therefore there is a relation between the Father and the Holy Spirit through the nature of love, and the same is true of the Holy Spirit who loves the Son and also Himself. And therefore I ask, whether in this loving, which the Holy Spirit has, there is a singular and common relation, from which follows the production of a person? Solution. In the loving of the Holy Spirit there is an amative relation, which is a proper and singular property of the Holy Spirit, namely, His active person in loving, and the passibility of His lovableness is with the amativitas one and the same person by essence, and the common relation which is of the lovableness of the Father and the Son, is thus a rest for the Holy Spirit, although it does not produce a person: just as for the Father and the Son, the common relation is a rest in producing the Holy Spirit. And in this passage there is much theology.

*On Questions of the relation of the celestial tree.*

**H**ow is relation in the sun? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. How is relation among Aries, Taurus, and Gemini? Solution. Aries is hot, Gemini similarly, and Aries actively, and Gemini passively: and their relation is in concordance through duality, and the relation which is threefold, is through the contrariety of Taurus, which with Aries has concordance through dryness, and with Gemini has contrariety through coldness and dryness: therefore Gemini is not as strong in Jupiter, as Taurus in Saturn. How is the relation between Mars and the Sun, who are of the complexion of fire? Solu-

--- Page 573 ---
# Questions of the leaves. 559

[Column 1]

Solution. Mars receives heat from Jupiter, & gives it to the sun, & the Sun gives it to Venus, who is of the complexion of Jupiter: therefore their relation is in concordance. And this same is true of the relation they have by contrariety against Jupiter & Venus, inasmuch as they are against humidity with their dryness, in which they have concordance. How do Aries & Libra relate to each other? Solution. Aries & Libra relate to each other through the first hour of day & night. Nevertheless, Raymundus said that he was not content with the positions of the ancients, who attributed the complexion of air to Libra, since Aries is in Spring in the complexion of fire: since it is so, that the proper hour of day is of the complexion of air, & the proper hour of night is of the complexion of earth.

*On Questions concerning the relation of the Angelic tree.*

How is relation in Angels? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Is there in an Angel the relation of the angelifying, the angelifiable, & to angelify? Solution. Because no Angel is from another Angel, but from itself, the aforesaid relation cannot exist in an Angel. Does the relation of equality which is between one Angel & another, indicate some positive entity, or is it merely intentional? Solution. No real relation exists outside substance. The relation which Saint Michael has in his will, of loving, & lovable, by loving himself, from what is it? Solution. Among other principles of Saint Michael's substance is a relation, one principle, which places with difference in the will power, object, & act, which are of its essen-

[Column 2]

-ce. And in this passage, there is much philosophy.

*On Questions concerning the relation of the Aeviternal tree.*

How is relation in aeviternity? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. How will a beatified body be subject to the relation of heating & heatable, with fire being heating & water heatable? Solution. At the head of aeviternity, relations are at rest, so that they can endure at the tail. How are the bodies of the damned in hell incorruptible, with their relations existing in contrary subjects? Solution. In the prison of justice, the consummabilities of the damned are imprisoned. Does the lovingness of Lucifer have its own lovable? Solution. If Lucifer had his own lovable, which would not be perverted into hatefulness, he would not have punishment.

*On Questions concerning the relation of the maternal tree.*

What is the greatest relation that God created between two persons? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. How could God create a greater relation of son & mother? Solution there. Without incarnation, could God create a relation in such great magnitude of love that it could not create a greater one? Solution there. What is the greatest relation that can exist between mercy & a sinner? Solution there.

De Quæstionibus actionis & paſsionis arboris vegetalis.

How in an apple are actions & passions of the elementary & vegetative power conjoined? Solution.
In a lamp, does the heat of fire move the heat of oil? which moves the matter of oil by the flame of fire.
Does the vegetative move the elementary in an apple or vice versa? Solution.
The ends of substances move principles & means, so that they themselves may be, & principles & means move parts, through which the ends are, & are that which they are.
In an apple, are actions & passions accidental or substantial? Solution.
Primary actions & passions are substantial, in which accidental ones are sustained, they themselves existing as instruments of the substantial ones.
In an apple, how can an accident have action & passion? Solution.
A hammer which moves a nail, is a substance, & insofar as its motion is by the hand, its motion is passive, & insofar as it moves the nail, it is active.

Through hearing, the memorative faculty is more active in the sensitive; and through seeing and speaking, the intellective; and through tasting, and through smelling, and touching, the volitive. Is fortitude a greater virtue through passion than through action? Solution. The passion of fortitude is stronger through charity and hope, and its action through faith, justice, prudence, and temperance. |

A certain Lady and her husband

the husband is jealous of that captive and

*On Questions of the action and passion*

How can action and passion be in the Most

Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. A certain Abbot
wants to eat chickens in the infirma-

ry, and gives a command to a certain Monk,
who says matins in the choir with

whether the Monk ought to be obedient
to the Abbot? Solution. No relative (thing/person)
has passion without great necessity.
A certain Abbot has fear of
poison, and gives a command to a certain Monk,
that he should bring him a dish, and
that he should eat first from that food, but
the Monk who receives the dish from the cook
does not know whether there is poison in the dish
or not. Now it is asked
whether the Monk ought to be obe-
dient to the Abbot in that case? Solu-
tion. A promise ought not to be made concerning any
uncertain thing. A certain Prior has money

and the convent have great necessity
of that money, because the convent
is in great debt. Now it is asked
whether the Prior ought to have a conscience
to give the money for marrying
his sister, or for the necessity
of his convent? Solution. He
who binds himself to service, gives passion
to all his goods.

*On Questions of Agriculture.*

What are the principles of agriculture? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since no mechanical art is as necessary as agriculture, why is the farmer less honored than another mechanic? Solution. According to the natural course, public utility is more desirable than special: therefore, he acts against nature who does not give more honor to the farmer than to the master who makes a tower or a ship. In which art are there more Philosophers? Solution. According to experience, no men know as much about Philosophy as farmers. In mechanical arts, what kind of men have greater hope? Solution. No mechanic has greater hope than the farmer, who sows grain and digs the earth.

*On Questions of Trade.*

What are the principles of trade? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How can a merchant be skillful in his art? Solution in the same place. Why do merchants have more money than other men? Solution. He who calculates what he spends and gains, and who often exchanges, has more money than another man. Why are merchants more lawful than other men? Solution. No mechanic has such a necessity for legality as a merchant.

*On Questions of Seafaring.*

What are the principles of seafaring? Solution. Go to the afore-

[Right Column]

mentioned. Which came first in conception, the oar or the sail? Solution. Because imagination first conceives movement from one place to another on land rather than on sea, and imagines that movement with the movement of feet, and not with the movement of wind, it imagines movement on the sea by oars before by sail, and a man who has no foot first imagines a hook, or a staff, on which he may be supported, so that he can move. Who was imagined before the ship, the sailor or the merchant? Solution. The first discerning sailor was a merchant, who desired to go by sea, so that he could earn money, therefore, trade is the cause of the art of seafaring. Why are sailors more audacious than other men? Solution. No men have fear so often as sailors.

*On Questions of Warfare.*

What are the principles of warfare? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Was warfare considered first by the judge than by the soldier? Solution. If the soldier considered warfare before the judge, he would not be an enemy of justice. Does the soldier consider the sword before the shield? Solution. In war, the sword is for wounding and killing, and the shield is because of the fear of death. Does the soldier consider the sword before the arrow? Solution. The sword is considered for audacity, and the arrow for fear.

On Questions of Law.
What are the principles of law? Solution.
Go to the aforementioned rubric. How
can a Jurist lead the positive science of law to necessary demon-
strations? Solution. Through the process of this
book, a Jurist can find and prove the truth
concerning those matters that pertain to the science
of law. Why does a Jurist
use the habit of memory more than the habit
of intellect, when it is the case that a Jurist
has greater concordance with intellect than with memory?
Solution. Jurists use the habit of memory more
than intellect, because the ancients founded the science
of Law upon the habit of memory. Therefore, it is a confused and pro-
lix science, and it is about particulars, by reason
of which confusion lawsuits last so long, and
certain Jurists are against others in diverse
opinions. A certain man made a will,
and said that if his wife, who was pregnant,
were to have a son, that he (the son) should have three parts
of all his goods, and his wife a fourth part; and if she were to have a daughter, the testator wished that his
wife should have three parts of all his goods,
and his daughter a fourth part. The testator
died, and the wife had a son and a daughter. Now it is asked
how many parts of the husband's goods the wife ought
to have? Solution. Between majority
and minority stands equality, and
that which is not in majority, nor
in minority, nor in equality, is nothing. The
woman is greater in her husband's goods through her daughter and lesser through her son: therefore, it is necessary that
she be equal in the goods, since she is in
them between majority and minority.
Therefore, it is necessary that the husband's goods be divided into eight
equal parts, of which the woman, the testator's
wife, ought to have three parts by reason
of her daughter, and one part by reason of her
son; and the son ought to have three parts,
and the daughter one. And thus the testator's will
is completed. The solution which Ray.
made greatly pleased the hermit, and he said that just as
Ray. solved that question with the princi-
ples of his art, which are majority, minority,
and equality, other questions of law
could be determined by natural reasons of law,
following the process of that art and this science.

On Questions of Medicine.
How are the principles of medicine?
Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric.
Why do more people die by
doctors than are cured? Solution.
Ibidem. How could the principles of medicine
be led to general principles?
Solution. The principles of medicine could be led to general principles according to this method:
fire is in pepper in the fourth degree
of heat, and earth in the third of dryness, and air
in the second of humidity, and water in the first.
And in cinnamon, fire is in the third
degree of heat, earth in the second of dryness,
and air in the first, and water is ungraded,
namely, if four parts are made of one degree,
water in cinnamon has only three parts. And in fennel,
fire is in the second degree of heat, and
earth in the first of dryness, and air has
in itself three parts of humidity, and water
has two parts of coldness. And in anise,
fire is in the first degree of heat, and
earth has in itself three parts of dryness,
and air has two of humidity, and
water has one part of coldness.
Therefore, fire is graded in the planets,
which are of their complexion in four ways,
and the same is true of air,
water, and earth, just as water in cam-
phor is in the fourth degree of coldness, and
air in the third degree of humidity, and earth
in the second of dryness, and fire in the first
degree of heat, and so in its own way for others.

Since each element has four kinds of degrees in plants, as indicated above, doctors can both arrange and make sixteen general electuaries, for example, from plants that are of the complexion of fire, from which four general electuaries can be made against the complexion of water through frigidity and humidity: such as one electuary that is in the fourth degree of heat, according to which pepper is, and another electuary in the third degree of heat, according to which cinnamon is graduated: and another in the second degree of heat, just as fennel is graduated, and another in one degree of heat, according to which anise is graduated. The four aforesaid electuaries of the complexion of fire having been thus arranged, doctors could make four electuaries of the complexion of air, and four of the complexion of water, and four of the complexion of earth: and thus doctors can have sixteen general electuaries for curing illnesses, which are through the four general qualities, so that if Martin's illness is by a fever, which is in the fourth degree of heat, the doctor ought to give against that heat that electuary which is of the complexion of water in the fourth degree of frigidity, and he ought to aid that degree of frigidity with the second degree of humidity of air, and with the first degree of dryness of earth. In a natural day there are twenty-four hours divided into four parts, and each part is appropriated to that element which is of its complexion: such as the triangle which is in the region from morning until midday, which is mostly of the complexion of air, and that triangle which is from midday until night, is of the complexion of fire, and that which is from sunset until midnight, is of the complexion of earth, and that which is from midnight until sunrise, is of the complexion of water. Therefore, illness reigns according to the aforesaid triangles, and according to whether the illness begins or ends in those four regions, the doctor can know the degree of the illness, as if a fever begins in the first hour of the day, it is in the first degree of humidity, and if in the second hour of the day it is in the second, and if in the third it is in the third: and if in the fourth it is in the fourth: and this according to a tertian fever, which is placed between hot and humid: but if the fever is simply tertian through choler, it will follow the order of midday...

*Concerning Questions of Philosophy.*

What are the principles of Philosophy?
Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. What is the order of Philosophy?
Solution. The order of Philosophy has been signified
in the process of this science.
Which science is more general? Solution.
Because Philosophy has more
general principles than other science,
therefore it is more general. Since Philosophy
is such a general science, why
are there not many Philosophers? Solution.
The intellect of a Philosopher labors more
than another's, and Philosophy does not
love money so much: as Law
and Medicine do.

*Concerning Questions of Theology.*

What are the principles of Theology?
Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric.
How can Theology be led to certain terms? Solution. This

[Column 2]

has been signified in the Christian
and divine tree. Why do Theologians use
position (assertion) more than ostension (demonstration)?
Solution. Position by belief is easy,
and ostension by understanding is difficult.
Raymond, do you believe that there will still
be a time, that Theology will be a
demonstrative science more than an assertive one?
Solution. In Theology there is more
truth than in other science, because
it has a nobler subject and its principles
were through prophecies, which are
of positions (assertions), and its means were through
miracles, which are remedies for illnesses,
and for truths: therefore it is necessary
that its end be of demonstrations:
for if it were not, God would do injury
to human intellect and to supreme
truth, and to the contemplation of both.

*Concerning Questions of the habit (disposition) of the
virtuous moral tree.*

What are the habits (dispositions) of virtues? Solution.
Go to the aforesaid rubric.
Why is Faith not a natural habit (disposition)?
Solution in the same place. One
man believes God exists, and believes that
He is good, infinite, and eternal, that
man studies so long in Philosophy and
Theology, that through study and through
the grace of God he attains God's existence through
necessary reasons, through which he attains
God's being good, infinite, and eternal,
therefore I ask, whether in that man there
is the habit (disposition) of faith? Solution. That
man who first believed God exists,
and afterwards understands God exists,
has the habit (disposition) of faith, but he does
not have it according to the manner in which he previously
had it: for then when he understands God,
he has the habit (disposition) of faith through
knowledge: just as a man who believes so that he
may understand, and could not understand
that object if previously in him not

is to love and understand God, than
merely to believe in God and not
understand Him, and the will can
love God more if the intellect contemplates
Him through understanding, than if
it contemplates Him only through belief.
And therefore, Theologians follow
the natural instinct and appetite for a
nobler end. And those speak ill
who say that man ought not to understand
the articles of faith, so that through his
credulity he might acquire merit, and through
greater merit, greater glory. And
inasmuch as they say this, they signify
that they are created for themselves, and not
for God, and they are ignorant of the merit
that the intellect has more through under-
standing than through belief: for it is more
weighty to inquire and find reasons and
demonstrations in understanding God to be,
than to positively believe God to be,
because the intellect, through understanding,
more strongly disposes the object to memory
and will, than through credulity.

On Questions of the Habit of the Vicious
Moral Tree.

How are the habits of vices?
Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric.
A man is in the habit of chastity,
and a beautiful lady passes before him;
that man, however, considers the pleasures
of lust, and his sensitive faculty feels
warmth. Because of that consideration,
I ask whether that man loses the habit
of chastity? Solution. The
habits of virtues and vices sometimes
participate in principles, whence that man
is touched by the habit of lust, and
is touched in the principle of the habit of chastity
according to the nature of the elemental,
vegetative, sensitive, and imaginative
tree, and that touch is represented
to memory and intellect, and after-
wards comes to the will; and if the
will consents, the habit of lust passes
through the middle and comes to its end, and
the habit of chastity has no beginning,
middle, nor end, in which it is
sustained. But if the will does not con-
sent, the habit of lust is outside the tri-
angle which it touches in the principles
we mentioned, and man is in the passion
of temptation and in the battle of virtue
and vice, and if he conquers, he has
merit, and if he is defeated, he has guilt.
Raymond, according to what you say, merit
or guilt comes from the will, after
it has chosen, or does not wish to choose.
And therefore, I ask, in what do the intellect
and memory, the imaginative, sensitive,
vegetative, and elemental faculties have guilt?
Solution. If memory and intellect
remain for a long time, and likewise
the imagination, on the object of lust,
the sensitive, vegetative, and elemental
faculties delighting in each other in that
delight, move the will to choose carnal
delight,

Whether there is habit in the Most High

not created, there was a habit in the
wisdom of God? Solution. No habit
can exist without the experience of some
part or the likeness of a subject, and
because the wisdom of God is infinite, a
likeness is not necessary for it,

that the sun continuously gives its likeness to

when it happens that Mercury does not

*On Questions of the habit of the Angelic tree.*

**H**abits Angelic, what are they? So-
lution. Go to the aforesaid
rubric. Does Saint Michael have the
habit of knowing Martin's sin?
Solution. Eyes have the habit of
seeing color, yet they cannot see it
without an instrument, nor can
Blessed Michael reach Martin's sin without Martin's works.
Does Lucifer have the habit of eternal
punishment? Solution. If Saint Michael did not
have the habit of eternal glory, the habit
of his glory would not be complete. Is
Lucifer's punishment as great as his
habits are? Solution. A logician knows only
as much about Logic as his Logical
habit is. And then the hermit said that
the punishment that Lucifer endures, no one
could narrate, nor write.

*On Questions of the habit of the Eternal tree.*

**H**abits eternal, what are they? So-
lution. Go to the aforesaid
rubric. The habits that the Saints have

[Right Column]

in eternity, in what way are they different
from the habits they had in this life?
Solution. The habits of the saints
are sound and not infirm, and they are free
and confirmed, and they proceed by affirmation
without negation and doubt.
But the habits of this life are infirm
and alterable from good to evil,
and from evil to good, and so with other
alterations according to the experience
we have. The logic that Martin knows,
will he know it in the other life? Solution.
If Martin is saved, he will have the logic
in habit, which he knew in this
life according to the end of beatitude
acquired through that habit, and if he is
damned, he will know it against the end,
so that he may endure punishment. Supposing that
Martin is saved, he having some virtue
in habit, more through intellect than
through will, will the will have as much
glory in habit as the intellect? Solution. Pur-
gatory is for this reason, that some
habit may be punished more than another, so that
they may equally have glory, never-
theless the King, through love for some
friend of his, spares that one's son, or his
brother.

**H**abits of Our Lady, what are they?
Solution. Go to the aforesaid

578 Questions of the leaves.

Does Our Lady use simply the habit of mercy, or with a means? Solution. If the hope that sinners have in Our Lady is an instrument, with which Our Lady has piety, it well follows that with the intellect with which she understands her Son, she understands sinners, and the hope they have in her. Does Blessed Peter have such great sanctity in habit that he can hold a place for his Vicar? Solution. With the sanctity of Our Lady, in which sinners have hope, many people are saved, and with the sanctity of their hope.

*Concerning Questions of the habit of the tree of Jesus Christ.*

Was there a habit of faith in Jesus Christ? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Did Jesus Christ have any temptation to sin? Solution there. Did Jesus Christ multiply species in His understanding? Solution. Every intellect that multiplies species is infirm. While Jesus Christ was in this world, did He forget? Solution. Just as God in Jesus Christ remembered as man, so man in Jesus Christ remembered as God.

*Concerning Questions of the habit of the divine tree.*

Whether there is habit in God? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. If there is no habit in God, how can He understand? Solution. God's intellect is pure act, both in understanding and in existing, nor is it necessary that His intellectivity understands with another intelligible, but with His own, which is of His essence: therefore, the divine intellect has a prerogative over every created intellect. Raymond, why do you deny that there is habit in God, since God is goodness and good, greatness and great, and so on for others? Solution. Raymond said that habit is that natural power in which an active power can act with another passive [power] in its own patient: just as fire, which has heat in habit, which with its heating capacity can act on its own heatable object with the aid of the heatability of the air: and therefore it is said that every habit is an accident, and not pure act, because it cannot act by itself without the aid of another: and because God does not need anything outside Himself, and has operation in Himself according to the production of the divine persons, therefore habit is denied in God, and it is said that His goodness, greatness, etc., are pure act in existing and in acting. If there were no production of persons in God, would there be habits in Him? Solution. If there were no production of persons in God, it would be necessary that His reasons would be habits and not pure act, just like His power, which could not empower itself, nor His eternity eternalize itself, and power would be empowering and empowerable by an external creature with whose aid it would relate to its empowerable object, and power would not have operation in itself, and the same is true of eternity, and the others.

*Concerning Questions of the habit of the exemplary tree.*

Why does God permit that one man be subject to another, since it is so that both are similar in species and in nature? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Why a beautiful Lady

A lady is proud because of her beauty, and a good lady is not proud because of her goodness, since it is so that goodness is more beautiful than the lady's face? Solution. No moral goodness participates in sin. How is moral goodness in a habit? Solution. A person who is morally good in habit has goodness, inasmuch as he follows the nature and reason of goodness, with which he produces good in some substance capable of being made good. How is fault a habit through sin? Solution. Through the privation of light is the habit of shadow, and through the act of sin is the habit of fault.

*Concerning Questions of Situs. And first concerning the elemental tree.*

What are the primary natural situations? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. How is the goodness of fire situated? Solution. The goodness of fire cannot be reached with the eyes, because it is not visible: but with imagination, its situation is imagined in the number of the bonifying, the bonifiable, and to bonify, which are of its essence, in which is its sustenance. How is the goodness of fire situated in magnitude? Solution. With the eyes, the magnitude of fire is not reached: but the extensiveness of goodness extended through magnitude is imagined: and through the great good, the bonifying and magnifying, and the bonifiable and magnifiable, and to bonify and to magnify. How is simple fire situated in the composite? Solution. Raymond said that that question should be made to the branches of the elemental tree.

[Right Column]

*Concerning Questions of Situs of the Vegetal Tree.*

How are the elements situated in the apple and the apple in them? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Are the elements below the vegetative or above? Solution. The elements and the vegetative are parts mixed together in the apple through a spherical body, namely round. Nevertheless, the vegetative is thus above the elemental: just as the end is above the beginning and the middle, and flame above oil. In the situation of the apple, does the vegetative place some extensiveness, which is of its nature? Solution. Let that question be made to a drop of vegetal oil, which extends itself over several drops of water aggregated from them, which extension it certainly could not make, if it were not of a corporeal nature. Why is fire in the apple not visible? Solution. No part that is in another is visible.

*Concerning Questions of Situs of the Sensual Tree.*

How are the elemental tree, and the vegetal tree and the sensual tree situated in a horse? Solution. Go to the leaves of the sensual tree. In a horse, does the sensitive, extended through it, place a corporeal nature, which is of its essence? Solution. If the sensitive were not a corporeal substance, it would not have the power to convert into its own species the heat of fire, nor its quantity, nor the taste of the vegetative, nor would the bones of the horse be in their own species. Is the common sense situated in the bones of the horse? Solution. If the common sense were not situated in the bones of the horse: the bones of the horse would not be of their own species. *On the Questions of the Situation of the Vicious Moral Tree.*

**H**ow is vice situated, since it is said to be a privation of virtue? Solution. The light which is at night before a person in a room situates darkness on the wall in a figure extended by that shadow. In a greedy person who sleeps, how is avarice situated? Solution. Just as the presence of light on the wall situates the likeness of that body which is between it and the wall, so the habit of avarice is situated by the dissimilarity of charity and generosity, which are deprived in the greedy person who sleeps or wakes. 582 Questions of the leaves.

**On the Questions of the site of the celestial tree.**

How is Heaven situated? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Is the Sun situated according to a circular or spherical body? Solution. No body is so full of circle, quadrangle, and triangle, as a body which is round. Why is the Sun situated in Saturn and the Moon? Solution. It is necessary that the nobler virtue be in the middle. Why is the Firmament situated in a circle? Solution. In a circular figure there is greater mobility than in another figure.

**On the Questions of the site of the angelic tree.**

How is the substance of an Angel situated? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How is the glory of good Angels situated? Solution. Ibidem. Is the Angelic site alterable? Solution. No substance is substantially alterable which, according to its nature, is neither in place nor in time. Does the situation of an Angel have a surface? Solution. In the spiritual distinction of one spiritual substance and another, there is a spiritual surface without contact and color.

**On the Questions of the site of the everlasting tree.**

How are the Saints situated in paradise, and the damned in hell? Solution. Raymond considered in the stars of heaven, and in the coals of a furnace, some of which are above others. And go to the aforementioned rubric. How are the souls of the damned situated in everlastingness? Solution. The intellect of a bad angel considered its punishment situated in despair. How are the habits of evil angels situated? Solution. Thus is punishment situated above guilt in everlastingness: just as heat above the substance of fire in inseparability. How is succession situated in everlastingness? Solution. The parts of a circle are situated in it without beginning, middle, and end of continuous quantity.

**On the Questions of the site of the maternal tree.**

How is Our Lady situated in heaven? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How is the will of Our Lady situated? Solution. Ibidem. How does Our Lady recall sinners, and how does she understand those who have hope in her? Solution. The Sun multiplies the heat of fire and its light: therefore fire is hotter and more luminous in summer than in winter, which Sun indeed we compare to the Lord Jesus Christ, in whom Our Lady has knowledge of those sinners who have hope in her. Is Our Lady standing in heaven, or is she sitting? Solution. No figure is as visible sitting as standing.

**On the Questions of the site of the tree of Jesus Christ.**

How is the situation of the divine and human nature in Christ? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since divine nature is infinite, how can it be situated in finite nature? Solution. Just as an Angel who passes through the middle from one place to another fecun

& if time exists at the beginning of that substance, its succession is not at the end. Are the species that Martin multiplies through recollecting, understanding, and loving, in the succession of time, or in an instant? Solution. If the phantasmatic species were the subject of motion, it would be necessary for it to be a substance; therefore, time exists in the successive motion of powers. Martin and the species he multiplies are in an instant without their motion: just as the white color of a black crow, which is in Martin's imagination in an instant, for he who imagines it, although that color of the crow does not move successively in time.

De Quæstionibus temporis arboris moralis virtuosa.

How is moral virtue in time? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Since charity is not a being subject to motion, how can it be in time? Solution. Aeviternity is not subject to motion, and it is in time from the part of the head, and not from the part of the tail. How does the time of charity begin and end? Solution. In the motion of the will which is moved to love God, is the beginning of charity in time, and when it is moved to love luxury, or another vice, is the end of charity, namely, its privation is in time. Martin has charity and justice when he uses charity, and he changes himself in using justice, how is his change in time? Solution. Martin considers the end of charity when he uses charity, and he considers the end of justice when he uses justice, and because one end is in one time, and another in another, that transmutation is in time by way of beginning, middle, and end.

De Quæstionibus temporis arboris moralis vitiosa.

How is vice in time? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. How do several vices exist at one time? Solution. Several vicious habits can exist at one time: just as vicious Peter, who at one and the same time can have the habit of avarice and of luxury, but at one and the same time he cannot actually use each, because the objects are diverse. When Peter uses luxury, how does the habit of avarice remain in time, after he does not use avarice? Solution. The habit of avarice exists while Peter uses luxury, inasmuch as it is a disposition and reason for Peter to use avarice in its own time. While Peter uses luxury and not avarice, how is the use of avarice in potency in future time? Solution. Peter's will is subject to the habit of avarice, which is in act, because the act of charity is deprived by it, and that habit of avarice is in the present time with the privation of charity and the lovable object which is external, through which avarice exists, in potency in future time, and when Peter acts under the habit of avarice, that lovableness exists in act in the present time.

De Quæstionibus temporis arboris Imperialis.

How is time in judgment? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. A knight sells a horse to a merchant; at that time when he sold the horse, it was sound, and the merchant tests the horse, and while he makes the horse run, the horse falls, and breaks its leg: now it is asked whether the sale is valid, or

EEee

--- Page 600 ---
**586 Questions of the leaves.**

not? Solution. In the sale of a horse, which
is sound, the elemental tree, nor the vegetal,
sensual, imaginal, nor rational tree does not err
on the part of the knight, and at the time
when the horse fell, the elemental, sensual,
and imaginal tree erred on the part of the horse
and the merchant, who was moving the horse:
therefore, according to justice, the sale is valid.
A certain merchant makes a will, and appoints
his son as heir, and leaves one hundred
solidi to Martin, the will having been published
in the absence of witnesses, and in the
presence of Martin, he says to his son that
Martin has two hundred solidi, and the
Scribe wrote two hundred solidi in the will
in the absence of witnesses, now it is asked
whether that will is valid, or not? Solution. The
will is not valid at the time of judgment, and
is valid at the time of agreement, which is
between the heir and Martin. Why can a
mute person not make a will? Solution. In a
mute person, the sensual tree errs, through
whose error time cannot be subject to him,
because speech cannot manifest the inner
conception to the relatives of the mute person,
therefore, with the figure of time failing, it is
necessary that the things ordered fail in the defect
of their figure.

**On Questions of the Time of the Apostolic Tree.**

IN the Most Holy Trinity, how can there
be production without time?
Solution. Go to the aforementioned
rubric. In the Most Holy Trinity, a principle
exists, insofar as the Father principiates the Son,
how can that principle be without time? Solution.
No suppositum in time is principiated which
is principiated from

***

the essence of the principle, which exists in eternity,
and not in time. At the time when the host is not
consecrated, how does the Sacrament of the altar
exist in future time? Solution. A judge existing
in his judgment uses the habit of justice, and the
amiability of temperance is in him in potential,
which is in act when the judge is at table, who
eats temperately. Why is usury? Solution. Through
usury, the five primary trees exist morally idle
in the usurious person, through which idleness
time and motion are not instruments for acquiring
virtues: therefore, Jews who are usurers are more
sluggish than other people.

**On Questions of the Time of the Celestial Tree.**

How is time without an artificial day?
Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How
is time without motion? Solution. Ibid. Why is
time? Solution. Ibid. How is simple time common
to past, present, and future time? Solution. Ibid.

**On Questions of the Time of the Angelic Tree.**

How is an angel in time? Solution. Go to the
aforementioned rubric. Was Saint Michael
principiatied in time in a corporal or spiritual
substance? Solution. If Saint Michael were
principiatied in time, which is a part of corporal
substance, time would be, which would be a part
of Saint Michael of the nature of corporal
substance. How can time be in one species, which
is corporal, and in another which is spiritual, and
that it be

Quæstiones foliorum. 587

[Column 1]

becomes one in itself? Solution. Just as
spiritual goodness and corporeal goodness
are essentially different, and are not
under one genus of real goodness,
so are the time of Saint Michael, and the
time of the sun, and the time of Martin’s
soul and his body, in difference; because
if it were under one genus of time,
they would participate in nature, and
spiritual substances would be partly of the
nature of the body, and corporeal [substances]
of the nature of the Spirit. How can an Angel
go from Rome to Jerusalem? Solution.
An Angel can go from Rome to Jerusalem
without time, inasmuch as its natural
time is not sustained in it, but inasmuch
as the Angel itself is originated in it:
and inasmuch as time is sustained
in Jerusalem and in Rome, an Angel
cannot go without time from one place
to another, time existing from the nature
of those places.

*On Questions of the time of the tree*
*of aeviternity.*

Will time in aeviternity be successive?
Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric.
Will this time of generation and corruption
have an end? Solution, same place. In
what time will the Antichrist come? Solution.
The Sun is in the midst of the planets,
so that it may commonly give them power,
and the advent of Jesus Christ is in the
midst of the beginning and end of the world,
so that it may give them completion:
therefore the Antichrist will come according
to this similitude at the end of the world,
so that he may be against the harvests of
the Lord Jesus Christ, and that he may be
further removed from His nativity. The
Antichrist who will have so much knowledge,
and who will know that he will act against
the truth, and that he will die in sin
because of what he will do, and

[Column 2]

will know his death, and that he would
remain in hell eternally, why will he do
evil? Solution. Just as the Lord Jesus
Christ related Himself to corporeal death
by reason of eternal life, so will the
Antichrist relate Himself to corporeal
death, so that he may relate himself to
eternal death, and he will do this so that
he may be more contrary to Him.

*On Questions of the time of the maternal*
*tree.*

At the time when Our Lady was conceived,
was she conceived in original sin?
Solution. Sin and virtue are contrary,
and because at that time when Our Lady
was conceived, virtue began to be more
strongly contrary to sin than in past time,
it is necessary that Our Lady was conceived
without sin. And go to the aforesaid rubric.
Is Our Lady always in the presence of her
Son, given that some say that she descends
to the lowest places through miracles, or
through aids to many persons? Solution.
The sun does not descend to the lowest
places, nevertheless its power is the cause
of generating flowers and fruits. Does Our
Lady recall the time in which her Son
was crucified and died? Solution. The
glory of Our Lady is so great that inasmuch
as she has such great glory, she does not
recall that time so as not to have sorrow,
but inasmuch as sinners have hope in her,
she recalls that time, and makes her Son
recall it, so that He may have mercy on
sinners. What is the nobler time that
ever was? Solution. The nobler time
that ever was, or will be, was that in which
Our Lady conceived her Son, because in
that time they united themselves together—
