finite and infinite nature, and God was made man, who participates with all creatures.

Of the Questions of the tree of time of Jesus Christ.

How can Eternity and time participate in each other?
Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since Jesus Christ was conceived and born in time, can he understand anything beyond time? Solution. Just as God sustained passion on the cross insofar as he was man, so Jesus Christ as man understands all things beyond time insofar as he is God. Is Jesus Christ in heaven always in one place? Solution. Greater glory is status and motion according to well-being, than of one only. In what time was God incarnated? Solution. Just as virtue is greater in the middle than at the extremes, it was necessary that the time in which Christ was incarnated should have been in the middle of the beginning and end of the world, so that it might have been proportioned with greater virtue.

Of the Questions of the tree of time of the Divine.

In that time in which God began the world, did he begin any novelty in himself? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How can God begin the world without any novelty of himself, he himself producing the world at one time, which he did not wish to produce before? Solution. In that time when God willed to produce the world, he willed to produce and create time, which could not be subject to anything that would have been before it, because if it could be, it would have been before it was, which is impossible. The Father gener-

[Right Column]
ates the Son, and the Son remains generable in eternity, in which eternity he remains generated, and this happens by way of production, namely, to produce the generated from generability. Now I ask, how can this happen without time? Solution. In this, that the generating agent is eternity, and from himself generates the generable, and to generate is a pure act, it follows necessarily to eternalize, in which time cannot exist. Could God create an eternal world? Solution. If the creator who is eternal could have created the world from his essence and nature, he could well have created the world eternally, so that in that creation there would have been neither beginning nor time. But because God cannot create the world from his nature, nor from his essence, the world could not receive the nature of eternity, nor can it be begun without time. And the same applies to the quantity it must have, which cannot be of the essence of infinite substance.

Of the Questions of the tree of time of the Exemplary.

Why do men desire to have sons? Solution. If men often considered that which a certain daughter of a King said to her Father, they would least desire sons. And go to the aforementioned rubric. Why does a father wish that his son be better than himself, and the Son desires to be this? Solution. Because the son is nearer according to time to the end of the world than the father, in which end the harvests are more perfect: naturally the son desires to be better than the father, and the father wishes the same thing. And in this it is signified that there will still be more holy persons. Why did the King desire more that from his gener-

--- Page 603 ---
Quæstiones foliorum. 589

[Column 1]

there should be more Kings of his lineage than of another lineage? Solution. Naturally, perfection consists in two things, namely in existing and acting: therefore naturally men desire to be, and that from their being another being should follow, and this successively, since it is so, that every cause loves its effect according to natural reason. A woman who had a son with such great labor, that she almost came near death, why does she again grant carnal union to her husband? Solution. Pains are forgotten, and pleasures are desired.

*About the Questions of the place of the elemental tree.*

[L] Ocus, what is it? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. How are things placed in a place? Solution there. What are the similarities of place that the eyes perceive? Solution there. Is place imaginable? Solution. Just as the essence of place is visible, so it is imaginable, and this is because the eyes do not perceive the essence of place, whence imagination imagines the similarities of place that the eyes perceive. But the intellect, above imagination, perceives the essence of place.

*About the Questions of the place of the vegetal tree.*

[I] N an apple, how are the vegetal and elemental tree placed? Solution. Go to the leaves of the vegetal tree. How is an apple that is potentially in an orchard placed? Solution. The end of the apple, which is placed potentially, is in the end of the orchard, which is in actuality. And the same is true of the goodness of the apple and the goodness of the orchard, and so of other first principles extended

[Column 2]

in roots, trunks, branches, twigs, leaves, flowers, and fruits elementally and vegetally. How is the color of an apple placed in the color of fire and other elements? Solution. Just as many parts are placed in their whole, so many colors are placed in the color of an apple aggregated from many. How can the vegetative power of an apple be placed in color, since it does not have color itself? Solution. Just as air, which is not hot by its nature, nor water: similarly their heat is situated in sensation; so the vegetative power of an apple, which does not have color according to its nature, is situated in the color of the apple which is properly from the elements, and which is appropriated to the apple.

*About the Questions of the place of the sensual tree.*

[I] N a horse, how are the elemental, vegetal, and sensual tree placed? Solution. Go to the leaves of the sensual tree. Does the sensitive faculty have a place that is of its own nature? Solution. Yes, a place is appropriated to the sensitive faculty through an elemental place, just as heat is appropriated to air through the natural heat of fire. If the sensitive faculty does not have a place by itself, how can it be placed in a place? Solution. Because created magnitude is capable of being made good, it can be made good, even though it is not good according to its nature, therefore it can be sustained in goodness insofar as it is good. How is the sensitive faculty placed in sensation? Solution. Naturally, sensation is disposed to be placed in the sensitive and in the sensible: just as air, which is disposed to be heated, insofar as it is capable of being heated, and because place, in a rough manner, consists of elements mixed with the vegetative and sensitive faculties of Martin's horse. Quæstiones foliorum. 591

[Column 1]

...nus of being luxurious, is the place in
which luxury exists in potential. From what place is luxury derived? Solution. Luxury is derived from the five primary trees, insofar as they are disposed to burn against chastity. That disposition by which the five trees are disposed to use luxury, from where does it come? Solution. It comes from the deviation of the liberty that God gives to man to do good, which liberty, indeed, which comes through man, is deformed, and is in potential, insofar as man is created from nothing.

On Questions concerning the place of the Imperial tree.

How ought a jurist use place in his judgment? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. A merchant who bought a horse, paid money in the absence of the horse, finally goes to the knight's house to receive the horse, which he finds dead, for which reason the merchant ought to recover the money: but supposing that another merchant bought a horse from another knight, who delivered the horse to him in the absence of money, and the knight going with him to the house, the merchant finds his chest broken, and the money stolen, nevertheless the sale of the horse is valid supposing that the merchant has the means to pay: therefore the question is, why is the latter sale valid, and not the former? Solution. In the merchant, the elemental tree remains abundant, although his money was stolen; but for the knight who lost the horse, the elemental, vegetal, sensual, and imaginal tree are lacking in a certain number of the horse. One man lent another a hundred talents, and said that he paid him fifty talents under a fig tree, but the debtor says,

[Column 2]

that he paid him a hundred under a chestnut tree, and each of them brought witnesses who say that the debtor paid all the talents under an apple orchard. Now it is asked according to which of the three trees the judge ought to give judgment? Solution. The plaintiff more often considers what he lends than the defendant what he receives as a loan, because money is more desirable to recover than to pay: therefore the plaintiff is more abundant in the imaginal and rational tree than the defendant, if nothing at all has been paid to him; and if everything has been paid to him, he is less abundant, because it has been paid to him, and the witnesses have greater concordance with the number of the elemental tree on the part of the defendant than on the part of the plaintiff, by which grea

**Concerning the Questions of the Place of the Maternal Tree.**

Sinners who have hope in Our Lady, how are they Sons of Our Lady? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Our Lady, how is she in heaven? Solution. Raymund imagined the star of dawn, which announces the coming of the sun. Our Lady, where is she in heaven? Solution. Raymund imagined the positioning of Angels and saints in the Empyrean heaven, and above that positioning, Jesus Christ, and he imagined Our Lady. The body of Our Lady which is in heaven, what sustains it? Solution. The Will wills, and its willing is complete.

**Concerning the Questions of the Place of the Tree of Jesus Christ.**

Is Jesus Christ in every place? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Human nature, how is it in the divine, since it is so that there is no place in the divine? Solution. Power can, and empowers, and the intellect can understand, and understands, and the will can love, and loves. Divine nature, which is infinite, how does it stand in human nature, which is finite? Solution. The greater virtue of the soul is in the virtue of the body, which is lesser, and from soul and body consists one person. Jesus Christ, how is he in heaven? Solution. Raymund imagined the sun, which illuminates the stars.

**Concerning the Questions of the Place of the Divine Tree.**

How is God in a place and without a place? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. God, how is he in himself? Solution. Goodness existing in its good-making, its good-receivable, and its act of making good, exists in itself. The world, how is it placed in God? Solution. Finite substance is placed in the infinite, inasmuch as it is terminated in it. Is God in Hell? Solution. If God were not essentially in Hell, it would be necessary that His substance be terminated and finite.

**Concerning the Questions of the Place of the Exemplary Tree.**

Power, wisdom, and will, how can they be without a place in goodness? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Is equality a place, or a subject through which power, wisdom, and will are equal in goodness in spiritual substance? Solution. So is equality a place of many equal forms, just as a place in an apple of many elements, and just as an apple which is the place of their composition. Divine forms, how can they be one in another without a place? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue. The whole, how is it placed in its parts, and the parts in it? Solution. In the same place.

**Concerning the Questions of the Quantity of the Celestial Exemplary Tree.**

Quantity, in which figure has more virtue? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. The sun is greater

594 Questions of the folios.

[Column 1]

than the Earth? Solution. If the sun illuminates the earth by straight lines according to the measurements which the ancients established, it is larger than the earth; however, if it illuminates the earth by illuminating Venus, and Venus Mercury, and Mercury the Moon, and the Moon fire, and fire air, and air water, and water the earth, the Sun illuminates the earth, multiplying the species of its splendor, and can be much smaller than the earth, (just as the flame of a candle, which is smaller than a room: and illuminates the room, multiplying its species). Why does the Sun appear larger in the morning than at midday? Solution. In the morning the vapors of the earth are of a grosser material than at midday, in whose grossness fire multiplies its likeness more than in less gross ones. Why is the Sun hotter at the hour of vespers than at the third hour? Solution. Just as the Sun multiplies its heat to fire, it multiplies its dryness to it, which it has greater, the more remote the Sun is from the earth, which is of the complexion of air.

*About the Questions of the exemplary quality of the angelic tree.*

Why does the Demon procure the sins of men, after he knows that because of their sins he has greater punishment? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. From what does fire live? Solution there. Why are there fevers? Solution there. Why does the demon not do good? Solution there.

*About the Questions of the exemplary action and passion of the maternal tree.*

Since the world is God's, why does it suffer that wolves eat sheep? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is there the Church? Solution there. Why is there religion? Solution there. Does the sinner have action in Our Lady, and Our Lady in her Son? Solution there.

*About the Questions of the exemplary habit of the Christian tree.*

Is there one idea, or more? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. From what does the habit of knowledge live? Solution there. How does man understand one thing with another? Solution there. How are necessity and contingency different, and how are they one and the same? Solution there.

*About the Questions of the exemplary site of the divine tree.*

Concerning the Questions of flowers. And first
concerning the elemental tree.

[Large initial F] What are the flowers of the elements? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. What are natural instruments? Solution ibid. How is the elemental an instrument of the elementer and the elemented? Solution. In writing, the pen is an instrument of the agent and the patient. And go to the rubric of virtue. Is "to ignite" an instrument for "that which is heated," or "to heat"? Solution. The pen is substantial to the letter, and its motion is accidental. Is "to ignite" an instrument for growing pepper, or "to heat"? Solution. "To ignite" is an instrument of elementing, and therefore it is an instrument of the substance of pepper, which substance indeed is from its instrument, and "to heat" is an instrument of the heat of pepper, and the heat of pepper is from its instrument. Is "to ignite" an instrument for feeling heat, or "to heat"? Solution. "To ignite" is a substantial instrument, which moves the substance to feeling, and "to heat" is an accidental instrument, which moves the substance to heat, and feeling is a flower, from which is born the felt thing, heated by heat, and elemented by fire, and sensed by feeling. How is fire an instrument for imagining? Solution. The flame of fire is visible, and its heat is sensible; therefore, fire is an instrument for imagination, inasmuch as it disposes the sensible object, from which imagination draws an imaginable likeness. How is fire an instrument for understanding? Solution. Fire produces the flame which is visible, and sense receives that visibility, the likeness of which imagination receives, and intellect receives that likeness from imagination, from which it assumes its understanding. How is fire an instrument for the will of man, which desires water? Solution. Fire multiplies its heat and dryness in the vegetative (faculty), and the vegetative gives that multiplication to the sensitive (faculty), and the imaginative receives the likeness of that multiplication, and the likeness of the passion, and it gives both likenesses to the intellect, which likenesses indeed the intellect represents to the will, which chose the desire for cold water against multiplied thirst. How does the individuation of substance and the sustenance of species occur? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric.

Concerning the Questions of the flowers of the
vegetative tree.

[Large initial F] Is the flower of the apple tree visible through the elementary or through the vegetative? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How is the flower an instrument of the fruit? Solution. In the sphere of the Moon, the elements collect the influence of celestial bodies, and fruits collect that influence from flowers. Is the apple in the flower of the apple tree in potential, or in the whole tree? Solution. In the flower are collected all the potentialities of the other parts of the tree. Why do flowers have more odor than leaves? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue. Why do flowers not remain on the tree as long as leaves? Solution ibid. Why do flowers have a more intense color than leaves? Solution ibid. Why does the fig tree not produce flowers? Solution ibid. Why are figs more pleasant to eat than other fruits? Solution ibid. Is fruit born from the apple successively or in

*Concerning the Questions of the flowers of the sensual tree.*

What kind of flowers are those of the sensual tree? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. In the sensual tree, which act is more general? Solution. Just as in pepper the more general act is to heat, rather than the act of other qualities, so in the sensitive tree, to sense is a more general act than the act of other trees. How are eyes instruments for seeing? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue. How is fire an instrument of the eyes and sight? Solution. Fire is an instrument of the eyes through elementing, and for sight itself through light. How is the vegetative faculty an instrument of the eyes and sight? Solution. The vegetative faculty is an instrument of the eyes by vegetating, and of sight by specifying the species that pertain to sight, just as in nourishing it specifies blood for the veins, and marrow for the bones. How is the sensitive faculty an instrument of the eyes and sight? Solution. The sensitive faculty is an instrument of the eyes in sensing, just as the elemental faculty in elementing, and the vegetative faculty in vegetating. And thus it is an instrument of sight by sensing, just as fire by illuminating, and the vegetative faculty by digesting. How is seeing an instrument of sight? Solution. Seeing is an act of active potency, which in it receives the likeness of passive potency. Why are there several tunics in the eyes? Solution. The multiplication of species occurs in giving a likeness

[Right Column]

to one potency from another, and therefore the center of the eyes signifies the sun, which gives its likeness to Venus, and the tunics signify other planets and spheres, which receive likenesses. Why do humans have pleasure in seeing beautiful figures, and displeasure in seeing ugly figures? Solution. Eyes and will have concordance in beauty and contrariety in ugliness. How the will does not want the eyes to see ugly things. And in this passage it is signified that the will is naturally beautiful. Why are the eyes more of the color of water and earth than of fire and air? Solution. In sight, the color of water and the color of earth are instruments of the color of fire and air: just as the motion of the hammer is an instrument of the motion of the nail in its action, or its operation.

*Concerning the Questions of the flowers of the imaginal tree.*

What are the flowers of the imaginal tree? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How is imagining an instrument of elementing? Solution. When imagining the delight of eating and drinking, imagination moves the sensitive faculty to feel the appetite for eating and drinking, and the sensitive faculty moves the vegetative faculty to vegetate, and the vegetative faculty moves the elemental faculty to element. And go to the rubric of virtue. How is the imaginative faculty an instrument of imagining? Solution. The imaginative faculty multiplies the likenesses of many things, and with all of them it imagines the likenesses of the desired image, so that it may be sensed or understood. When the imaginative faculty imagines a castle or another object, how is imagining an instrument? Solution. *Concerning the Questions of the Flowers of Fortitude.*

What is the Flower of Fortitude? Solution.
Go to the aforesaid rubric. How is the Flower
of Fortitude? Solution. Just as it is in
scripture, that the will moves the hand, and the
hand the pen, and the pen letters to those external
figures, which are internally imagined and concei-
ved, so is the merit of fortitude
in strengthening good habits
conceived within the dispositions of virtues.
What utility does the merit of fortitude
bring? Solution. Fortitude brings victory
and fame and peace, and in the other
life, the confirmation of eternal rest.
Can fortitude be overcome? Solution.
Nothing overcomes fortitude except man,
whose part it is, who overcomes it,
insofar as he does not wish to use it.

in sustaining a man. Why is temperance more
attributed to eating itself than to another

in one subject than in another, so any
virtuous habit has a more proper
subject, insofar as it more

another. How can man understand
and imagine temperance in

of healthy forms.

*Concerning the Questions of the Flowers of Faith.*

What is the Flower of Faith? Solution. Go
to the aforesaid rubric. How does
faith endure? Solution there.
Which is the nobler flower, to believe or
to understand? Solution. In understanding
that which understands truth about God, there
is a greater magnitude of goodness than in
believing that which believes truth about God;
in which believing there is a greater magni-
tude of goodness than in understanding
that which understands that an ox and an ass are not
of one species. Is the merit that
a man has through faith as great,
as the merit that a man has through
understanding? Solution. No sick person
can render as much service as a
healthy person.

mercy. With which virtue does hoping

Justice and charity assure judging
and remitting of necessity through hoping.

*On the Questions of the flowers of charity.*

**F**lower of charity, who is it? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric.
What are the tunics of loving? Solution, there. Why is loving greater by giving than by receiving? Solution. Fire is noble and stronger by heating than by drying. Is disliking a vice as noble as loving a virtue? Solution. No consequent is as noble as its antecedent.

*On the Questions of the flowers of vices.*

**F**lowers of vices, what are they? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. From what does sinning come? Solution. Sinning comes from the deviation of the beginning and the middle from the end for which they exist. Where did guilt begin? Solution. Guilt began in the idleness of reasons against the diligence of virtue. What is the consequence of guilt? Solution. The consequence of guilt is punishment, just as the consequence of moral virtue is glory. How are elementary, vegetative, sentient, and imaginative things clothed in guilt? Solution. In the privation of the end is the loss of instruments. How is remembering to sin? Solution. To remember God and not to love Him for His goodness is to sin. How is understanding to sin? Solution. To understand sin and not to dislike it is to sin, and therefore no one ought to speak of the sin they have committed with laughter, but with contrition and sorrow. How is loving to sin? Solution. Loving is to sin when it is an act of the will without charity. How is fear to sin? Solution. Fear is to sin when

[Right Column]

it is not a consequence of loving clothed in charity. How is conscience to sin? Solution. Conscience is to sin without contrition.

*On the Questions of the flowers of the Imperial tree.*

**F**lowers of the Prince, what are they? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. In what can judging and injuring be more? Solution, there. In what can honoring or dishonoring ascend higher? Solution, there. In what can glorifying and tormenting be greater? Solution, there. Of what can praising and cursing be better narrated? Solution, there. In what can speaking truth and lying be found more quickly? Solution, there. In what do taking away and giving more often go to stand? Solution, there. In what can being proud and being humble differ more? Solution, there. Who can give a good and bad example more? Solution, there. In what can loving and disliking ascend more? Solution, there.

*On the Questions of the flowers of the Apostolic tree.*

**F**lowers of the Apostolic tree, what are they? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. What is an article? Solution. An article is a testimony of truths through belief or through understanding. Which are the higher and more beautiful flowers? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue. Why does the Holy Church weep? Solution. The Holy Church weeps because its flowers throughout the whole world are not remembered, known, and loved.

Quæstiones florum. 603

[Left Column]

More justly, those who communicate themselves in such a great substance through loving: just as there is a substance which is through generating, it is necessary that the third person be called the Holy Spirit. And go to the second reason of the aforementioned rubric. Can there be a greater relation than between the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit? Solution. In the essence and nature of love, there cannot be more proper or more essential properties than lovability, amiability, and loving. Therefore, love is greater through such a relation than through other properties which are not of the essence and nature of love. Similarly, between the producer and the producible, which is of the essence and nature of the producer, there cannot be a greater relation in production than between the Father and the Son, nor can the concordance of both be greater than in loving. Can there be a greater concordance than that of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit? Solution. No concordance can be greater in goodness than between the one who makes good, the one who can be made good, and the act of making good; nor in greatness than between the one who magnifies, the one who can be magnified, and the act of magnifying; nor in eternity than between the one who eternizes, the one who can be eternized, and the act of eternizing. And if there could be a greater concordance than between the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit in goodness, and so for the others, there could be a greater concordance between the one who makes good, the one who can be made good, and the act of making good, with the one who can be made good not existing from the nature and essence of the one who makes good, nor the act of making good from the essence and nature of both, which is impossible. Can there be greater equality than that of the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit? Solution. In the essence and nature of power, there cannot be greater equality than between the one who empowers, the one who can be empowered, and the act of empowering.

[Right Column]

And the same is true for the essence of principle, in which there cannot be greater equality than between the one who originates, the one who can be originated, and the act of originating: because, if the one who empowers could more equally make equal to itself that which can be empowered of another essence and nature than its own, it would have a greater disposition to act from its equality in an essence and nature which was not of its own kind, than that which was of its own kind, which is impossible. And because the one who can be empowered, which is of the essence of the one who empowers, is the Son, since he is produced from him, and the one who empowers is the Father, consequently the act of empowering of both is the Holy Spirit. Therefore, there must be the greatest equality that can exist, of Paternity, Filiation, and Spiration.

604	Questions of flowers.

**On Questions of creation.**

Is the world eternal, or was it created anew? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Could God create the world eternal? Solution. It is impossible that the power of God could do more concerning eternity than concerning goodness, greatness, wisdom, will, truth, glory, and virtue, because if it could do more through eternity than through other forms, it would have a greater suitability with eternity than with other forms, and there would be in God a greater and lesser suitability, which is impossible: therefore the power of God cannot produce nor create the world in the infinity of goodness, greatness, power, wisdom, and so on for other forms, because the world could not receive that infinity, but power could give it, if the subject were disposed to receive it: wherefore just as power cannot make the world infinite through goodness, greatness, and so on for other dignities, so it cannot make it infinite through eternity. And go to the rubric of virtue. If the world were eternal, what would follow? Solution. If the world were eternal, and not created anew, its eternity would be the end and completion of all parts of the world, and God's eternity would not, since it is so that the infinite has no need of another infinite, and thus it would follow that God would not be the end and completion of the world, and that the world would have its end in itself, which is impossible and against the nobility of God. Also another inconvenience would follow, which you will find in the second reason of the aforementioned rubric. If the world were eternal, would it be better than if it were new? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue to the third reason. What derogation would there be to God, if the world were eternal? Solution there to the fourth reason. If the world is created, from what is it originated? Solution. The wisdom of God, which is infinite, and which comprehends both future, present, and past things, understood the world before it existed, and the will of God willed that the world should be originated and produced, according to what was understood by wisdom, and the power of God made it possible and completed it; and put into act that which the will willed, and so the world was created in this manner, and it was not created from anything, and because it was not, it is said that it was created from nothing.

And go to the rubric of virtue to the second reason. If sin had not originated in the first parents, what inconveniences would follow? Solution there to the third reason. The contrariety which is through sin against the concordance which is through virtue, how is it known that it originated in the first parents? Solution

*On Questions of recreation.*

Is the world recreated? Solution.
We intend to prove the incarnation
and death of Jesus Christ, and from
the proof of these two articles
it follows that the world is recreated,
God being incarnate and dead, insofar
as He is man, so that the world might be
recreated. Supposing that God is
incarnate and dead, why does it follow
that the world is recreated? Solution.
For sin, satisfaction is required, and
through the sin of the first man, the world
was deviated from the end for which it was
created, and by the death of a more general
man in magnitude of goodness,
holiness, and virtue, for whom the world
was created, who is Jesus Christ, His
death made satisfaction, and restored the world
to the end for which it was created: and
if His death had not been sufficient for the satisfac-
tion of general sin, He would be deficient
in magnitude of goodness, and Adam
would be greater in the production of evil
than Jesus Christ in the reparation of good,
which is impossible, since Jesus Christ
is God and man. Jesus Christ,
insofar as He is God, was not
dead, therefore God did not recreate the world
through death, and therefore I ask,
whether the humanity of Christ is sufficient
for recreating the world? Solution.
God is so perfect in the magni-

dignities that in this, that He is

of the world through His death, although the deity

*About the Questions concerning Jesus being con-*
*ceived, and God being incarnate.*

Is God incarnate? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. If God were not incarnate, what inconveniences would follow? Solution. If God were not incarnate, His reasons would at all times desire to have rest in creatures, and would never attain it. And go to the second reason of the aforementioned rubric. Why is God incarnate? Solution. God is incarnate so that He might produce a greater concordance that can exist between the cause and its effect. And go to the rubric of virtue, to the third reason. If God had not been incarnate, could His nature be the end and completion of created nature? Solution, ibid., to the fourth reason. If God were not incarnate, could His reasons be the end and completion for created reasons? Solution, ibid., to the fifth reason.

*On Questions of the flowers of the Angelic tree.*

**W**hat are the flowers of the angelic tree? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Does a Seraph touch God naturally, or supernaturally? Solution there. Does a Seraph understand God with a medium, or without a medium? Solution there. How is the love of a Seraph equally endowed with magnitude and goodness? Solution. In the power of a Seraph's love, goodness, magnitude, and its will are equally communicated. Why are the understanding and love of a Seraph equal in the magnitude of goodness? Solution. The goodness and magnitude of God are equally intelligible and lovable. Why does a Seraph love God more than itself? Solution. In the Empyrean heaven, greater lovableness more strongly moves one to love a greater object of love than a lesser one. Can a Seraph be ignorant? Solution. Eyes that are open by day cannot fail to see, and God being the exemplar of a Seraph, a Seraph cannot be ignorant. Can a Seraph love God more at one time than at another? Solution. The will of a Seraph is so full of beatitude that its love cannot grow, nor diminish. Does God love one angel as much as another? Solution. A sunbeam is as communicable according to its nature to small windows of a room as to large ones, but the small ones cannot receive as much clarity from it as the large ones. Does the understanding of an angel illuminate the understanding of a human? Solution. Between understanding and loving there is naturally a concordance, and an angel represents to Martin some lovable object, and if Martin loves that...

[Right Column]

...tin, the will of the angel and the will of Martin have a concordance in that lovableness, by reason of which the angel illuminates Martin's intellect with the intelligibility of the object through both [the angel and Martin] loving [it].

*On Questions of the flowers of the eternal tree. And first, on glory.*

**W**hat are the flowers of the eternal tree? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How is heavenly glory good? Solution there, to the first paragraph. How great is the goodness of Paradise? Solution there, to the second paragraph. With what does the goodness of Paradise endure? Solution there, to the third paragraph. How can the goodness of glory exist? Solution there, to the fourth paragraph. How is the goodness of glory understood? Solution there, to the fifth paragraph. How is the goodness of glory lovable? Solution there, to the sixth paragraph. How does the goodness of Paradise have virtue? Solution there, to the seventh paragraph. How is the goodness of glory in truth? Solution there, to the eighth paragraph. Of what is the glory of Paradise? Solution. The glory of Paradise is of the acts of divine, angelic, and human reasons, which acts are indeed three lights of glory, which mingle in eternal glorification without ceasing. And by this step, it is known how great is the glory of Paradise.

...great reason for God, that He would produce so great a creature in goodness, that goodness could not be a greater reason?
Solution. Go to the rubric of the goodness and greatness of the incarnation.
Why did God not assume the nature of multiple creatures?
Solution. Just as in God, goodness can be a greater reason for God, that He produces a great good, God being one and not multiple, so there is a greater reason for God existing incarnate, and as one man, than if He were incarnate in multiple creatures.
Is the goodness of God a reason for God, that He should produce an eternal created good?
Solution. So eternity is a reason for God, that He produces a creature in eternity, just as goodness is a reason, that He produces a creature in goodness. But just as created goodness cannot be produced in infinity, so the duration of a creature cannot be produced without time, and because created duration can be produced in eternity through the incarnation, man existing as eternal God, supreme goodness requires that man be God and the highest good.

On Magnitude.

How are Magnitude and eternity
greater reasons of the creature? Solution. In the person who is made of
divine and human nature, Magnitude and eternity are greater reasons
of the creature. And go to the aforementioned rubric.
How can the divine person endure in one state, who at one
time was man, and at another time was not man? Solution. No
change can be in eternal and infinite nature.
Through magnitude and power, how is the incarnation proven?
Solution. Go to the rubric of magnitude of power.
Magnitude and power, which are reasons of God, how
do they require equal acts in creatures? Solution. Power requires from
magnitude such a great act, namely to magnify:
just as it can make possible and illuminate the act, namely
to make possible, magnitude requires from power according to magnifying,
and these two requirements must be sustained in the incarnation.

Questions of flowers. 617

Concerning the Questions of the flowers of the tree of Jesus Christ.

Concerning Power.

**H**ow is the incarnation proven by power and wisdom?
Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric.

The wisdom of God, which knows that power can make me Pope, does it follow because of this that it will make me Pope?
Solution. The wisdom of God does not consider any superfluous idea, so that in its consideration there may not be an emptiness of purpose.

How are divine power and divine will causes of the incarnation?
Solution. Go to the rubric of will and power.

Since the will of God can will more incarnations through more men, does it follow because of this that they exist, after the will can love them?
Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue.

By what means can the power of God use corporal power as much as spiritual?
Solution. Go to the rubric of the power of virtue.

If there were no incarnation, would the power of God be idle and faulty?
Solution. If there were no way by reason of which divine power could communicate itself as much to corporal substance as to spiritual, it would be idle in that way.

How do "to make possible" and "to verify" cause the incarnation?
Solution. Go to the rubric of the power of truth.

Since the power of God is infinite, what compels it to communicate itself through incarnation?
Solution. The Judge is free in his judging, and because truth is his reason for making a true judgment, the Judge compels himself with the reason of justice and truth to give a true sentence against falsehood and injustice.

Since the power of God is glorious by itself, what glory is the incarnation to it?

[Column 2]

Solution. Every cause takes delight in producing its likeness, although without that production it is perfect by itself. And go to the rubric of the power of glory.

How does divine glory compel divine power to make the incarnation possible?
Solution. Power being the reason for making possible, and glory for glorifying, God equally compels Himself (so to speak) in creating, with His reasons, to incarnate Himself, just as with His mercy He compels Himself to forgive.

Concerning the Will.

How are divine will and virtue reasons for a greater creature, which can be created? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why does divine will love a great virtue more than a small virtue? Solution. Since divine will is great, and not small, it would be a fault for it if it loved a small virtue more than a great one. Why does divine will love a greater truth more than a lesser one? Solution. Go to the rubric of the will of truth. Since divine will is great and not small, why does it love a small truth? Solution. According to the comparison of truth and will, divine will loves small truth as much as great truth: but because divine will is great and not small, according to the nature of its greatness, it cannot love small truth as much as great truth. In what are the end of God and the end of the creature more strongly removed from falsity? Solution: Ibid.
Between God and the creature, how can there be truth in such great majority that it could not be greater? Solution: Go to the rubric of the majority of truth.
How is divine truth a cause for a greater majority? Solution: Because divine truth is great and not small, it is a cause for greater creatability.
How are truth and equality causes of the incarnation? Solution: Divine truth is great, and not small, and the same applies to divine equality, which is concerning persons: therefore they have concordance in majority.
How can God love the creature with a greater loving, and how can He verify it with a greater verifying? Solution: Go to the rubric of the equality of truth.
If there were no incarnation, what would follow concerning created verification? Solution: Go to the rubric of the minority of truth.

of Jesus Christ.

On the Middle.

Without incarnation, could there be a created
and particularized middle, the form and
end of all created middles?
Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How
could God exalt one accident with such great
virtue that it would be the end of every
created substance?
Solution. Ibid. How can the middle
be placed in a greater greaterness of virtue?

middle. Could a greater greaterness be created without in-
carnation? Solution. If there were no
incarnation, a greater greaterness could not
be placed in creation. Without incar-

greaterness, namely that it be of the beginning and the end?

could fire be heated by water, and
how could light be the occasion of

created production moved from a

*On the Questions of majority which*
*is concerning the flowers of the tree of Jesus*
*Christ.*

How is common utility the cause of incarnation? Solution. Common utility and majority have a proportion with the magnitude of goodness. How does common utility have a greater proportion with majority than with equality, since it is about equal things? Solution. Common utility is sustained in the exaltation of a greater majority in the magnitude of goodness. When God created the world, could God have before Him without incarnation a greater majority than a lesser one? Solution. Go to the rubric of majority and minority. Why is it more fitting for God to create a greater creature than a lesser one? Solution. Magnitude and majority have concordance, and smallness and minority, therefore incarnation is signified to be of necessity.

*On the Questions of equality concerning the flowers of the tree of Jesus Christ.*

How are equality and majority causes of incarnation? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. If there were no incarnation, what would follow concerning created equality? Solution ibid. We have proven the incarnation, and we have given doctrine according to the general art, how with the primary forms of this science man may know how to inquire and find truth, mixing one principle with another as we have done, and applying them to one question, and just as we have responded to some objections made against the incarnation, one can respond according to the method we have held to many other foreign objections. And this is a general rule throughout this entire science.

*On the Questions of divine productions.*

According to what we have made questions concerning the incarnation of God through the primary forms, we wish to make questions concerning the production of divine persons, and first through goodness, magnitude, and eternity. How are goodness, magnitude, and eternity reasons for divine production? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. If there were no production in God, could there be reasons in Him? Solution. If the antecedent is destroyed, the consequent is destroyed. If there were no production in God, could there be action in His power through goodness, magnitude, and eternity? Solution. goodness is the reason for good, that it may produce

of necessity, after it understands goodness,

that it may produce good, and great
good, and the same through eternity. And
if production were not in God, it would understand
goodness to be an idle reason, whence evil would follow and
a smallness of goodness, and many other inconveniences
would follow, which cannot be in the divine
essence. The divine will,
how is it a necessary reason for production?

of necessity? Solution. Because goodness,
greatness, eternity, and truth are
reasons *propter quid*, and are what
they are by form, production in God
is of necessity. And go to the
rubric of virtue. Glory, how
is it a reason *propter quid* for goodness, greatness
and eternity? Solution. Go to the
rubric of goodness, greatness,
eternity, and glory. Without production,
could eternity have great glory of goodness?
Solution. The privation *propter quid* concerning eternity would be deprived
of that great glory of goodness itself.
Eternity, how can it be great in
goodness? Solution. Go to the rubric
of goodness, greatness, eternity, and
difference. Could to produce be in
God without distinction of the producer and
the produced? Solution. Just as contradiction
does not sustain that the produced and he
who produces are one and the same in
number, so goodness, greatness, eternity
of production do not sustain that there be
production without distinction of the produced
and of him who produces that produced thing.
Concord, how does it require
production from goodness, greatness
and eternity? Solution. Inasmuch
as goodness and eternity are reasons

is the reason for production. And go to the
rubric of goodness, greatness, eternity,

...it would multiply the species, and thus create a chimera outside of truth: just as men do, and the will would love a fourth person to exist in truth or in falsehood. Hence, supposing that a fourth person cannot exist in God, power cannot consider a fourth person. Since power is glory, how can it have action in glory? Solution. Refer to the rubric on power, wisdom, will, and glory. Since the Father and the Son are productive persons, and the Holy Spirit is not a productive person, how can it have as much glory as the Father and the Son? Solution. Because the Holy Spirit is of the entire productivity of the Father and the Son, and is of their entire glory, it is as glorious as the Father and the Son, although it does not produce a person. How is divine power free in wisdom and will? Solution. Refer to the rubric on power, wisdom, will, and difference. Without distinction, could divine wisdom in the will know the number one, two, three: just as in the will it knows the number of the lover, the beloved, and to love? Solution. Everything that is not intelligible is impossible. Since power, wisdom, and will are one and the same in number, how can they have concordance? Solution. Refer to the rubric on power, wisdom, will, and concordance. Since power and wisdom have concordance in knowing sin, why do power and will not have concordance in willing sin? Solution. Sin is knowable by reason of justice, and it is not lovable, because evil is contrary to goodness, which is numerically identical with the will. Why can there be no contrariety in God? Solution. Refer to the rubric on power, wisdom, will, and contrariety. Since

[Column 2]

there is no contrariety among God's power, wisdom, and will, why did God create contrariety? Solution. If God had not created contrariety under the aspect of proper qualities and diverse ends, there could be no corruption in number, nor consequently generation, and genera and species would be without individuals, and virtues and vices would not be contrary, nor punishment and glory: therefore God created contrariety under the aspect of proper qualities of diverse ends, so that there would be no emptiness of purpose in the entire created universe. How can the principle be more intelligible and more lovable in God? Solution. Refer to the rubric on power, wisdom, will, and principle. Since God is eternal and infinite, how can He originate the Son and the Holy Spirit from Himself? Solution. Because in God there is actual positivity and possibility, the capacity to know and knowability, the capacity to love and lovability, there is in God actual principiating power and principiability. How can there be a medium in God's power? Solution. Just as in wisdom there can be understanding through itself, and through power, and through the will, which loves that understanding, so in power there can be the capacity to effect through possibility, knowability, and lovability. And refer to the rubric on will, power, and medium. Since in God the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are one simple essence without quantity, how can the Holy Spirit be in the midst of the Father and the Son? Solution. In divine love, there is loving in the midst of the lover and the beloved without quantity. What is the end of power? Solution. Refer to the rubric on power, wisdom, will, and end. ...principality, which can exist. Why is a medium necessary for the glory, virtue, and truth of God? Solution. Refer to the rubric of virtue, truth, glory, and medium. How is virtue a medium between truth and glory? Solution. Virtue is a medium between glory and truth by giving to each equally its likeness in verifying and glorifying. Without production, could any divine reason attain its end? Solution. Refer to the rubric of virtue, truth, glory, and end. Without production, how would divine reasons be empty without it? Solution. If one were to draw from glory the glorifier, the glorifiable, and the act of glorifying, no end could exist in glory. How can virtue and truth exist in glory in the greatest greatness that can be? Solution. Refer to the rubric of virtue, truth, glory, and greatness. How can virtue communicate itself in greater glory and truth? Solution. The greater communication of virtue is that it consists of the producer, the producible, and the act of producing, which are the same virtue. How can the act of truth be sustained in glory? Solution. Refer to the rubric of virtue, truth, glory, and equality. Inequality, with what and by whom, is further from the virtue, truth, and glory of God? Solution. Nothing is as contrary to inequality as equality. Can truth have a pure act in glory, in virtue, and in itself without production? Solution. Refer to the rubric of virtue, truth, glory, and lesser-ness. How is a greater act of virtue further removed from a greater act of vice? Solution. No act is as far removed from a lesser act of virtue as the greatest act of virtue that can be.

**On Questions of Distinction, Concordance, and Contrariety concerning the Flowers of the Divine Tree.**

How are divine reasons more removed from idleness? Solution. Refer to the aforementioned rubric. How are distinction and contrariety more contrary? Solution. That distinction which is in concordance, and which is concordance, is more removed from contrariety than any other distinction. Why is principia-bility in God by necessity? Solution. Refer to the rubric of distinction, concordance, contrariety, and principle. In principle, how is distinction further removed from contrariety? Solution. In that distinction which is concordance, contrariety does not have any condition of a principle. Without the production of concord, could contrariety exist in God? Solution. In a distinction in which there is no condition of concordance, it is necessary that there be contrariety. And refer to the rubric of distinction, concordance, contrariety, and medium. How are distinguishing and concord-ing a medium in inspiring? Solution. To judge clothed in charity is a medium in love. How is the end of concordance in the Godhead without contrariety? Solution. Refer to the rubric of distinction, concordance, contrariety, and end. If in the will of God there were no distinction of the lover, the lovable, and the act of loving, what would follow? Solution. If in the will of God there were no distinction of the lover, the lovable, and the act of loving, in it there could be neither end nor concordance. Why is distinction naturally greater in concordance than in contrariety? Solution. Refer to the rubric of distinction, concordance, contrariety, and LLII

--- Page 648 ---
634		Questions of the flowers.

greaterness. How are the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit in the greatest greaterness of distinction and concordance? Solution. The Son existing from the whole Father, and the Holy Spirit existing from both without any condition of contrariety, their distinction and concordance is in the greatest greaterness that can be. How is the concordance of God more remote from contrariety? Solution. Go to the rubric of difference, concordance, contrariety, and equality. If there were no equality in God, would it be necessary for there to be contrariety in Him? Solution. If in God there were not the equality of equalizing, being equal, and to equalize with distinguishing and concord, from its privation would follow the habit of contrariety in the essence of God. How can concordance and distinction be in God without minority? Solution. Without accident, no minority can exist. And go to the rubric of difference of concordance, contrariety, and minority. Since the Father is producing, and the Son similarly, how can the Holy Spirit, who does not produce, be in such great distinction and concordance, as are the Father and the Son? Solution. The two passions of the Holy Spirit are from the whole activity of the Father and the Son, and thus they are one person, just as two activities are one principle.

*Concerning the Questions of principle, middle &*
*end concerning the flowers of the divine tree.*

How can God be a pure principle? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since the Holy Spirit is from the Father, and the Son, how is He as much from the Son as from the Father? Solution. In the unity of the middle, and the end, is the unity of the principle. How can principle, middle, and end be in the greatest greaterness that can exist? Solution. Go to the rubric of principle, middle, end, and greaterness. Since there is no emptiness in God, how can there be completion in Him? Solution. Thus it is necessary that in God there be completion from the completer and the completable: just as in love, to love from the lover and the lovable. How can the originating, the originatable, and to originate be equal in the middle and in the end? Solution. Go to the rubric of principle, middle, end, and equality. How are principiativity and principiability equal in originating? Solution. Let this question be made for infiniting, eternizing, generating, and spirating. If in God there were not pure originating, what would follow from this? Solution. Go to the rubric of principle, middle, end, and minority. How is knowledge had of greater and lesser originating? Solution there.

*Concerning the Questions of greaterness, equality,*
*& minority.*

With what are the divine persons removed from greaterness and minority? Solution. In the eternal and infinite, greaterness and minority cannot exist to equalize. And go to the aforementioned rubric. If there were no equality in God, would there be inequality in Him? Solution. He who would deprive God of one reason, would deprive Him of all reasons.

Solution. In natural things there are simple forms, so that they may be composite. Whether there is a general elemental fruit? Solution. If there were no general vegetation, no plant would exist. Solution. Inasmuch as a serpent kills men, it is an instrument of God's justice
and of human prudence: it also has
some conditions which are good for human conditions: such as theriac,
which is made from a serpent, which is good
against poison, against leprosy, and
against the falling sickness (epilepsy), and it strengthens natural heat.

*Concerning Questions of the Fruit/Product of the Imaginal Tree.*

What is the fruit/product of the imaginal tree?
Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. From what is the fruit/product of the imaginal tree? Solution in the same place. What is the fruit/product of imagination? Solution. It is by form, and by end: by form,
that is, by imagining: by end, that is, by the imagined thing. A goat imagines a wolf of which it has fear: therefore it is asked, how is the wolf, which is imagined, the product of the goat's imagination? Solution. Primary products arise from secondary intentions: just as a goat which has fear of a wolf, because it loves to live. A goat imagines a spring: how is the imagined spring the product of the goat's imagination?
Solution. The likeness of the spring which imagination multiplies, is the secondary product of imagination, and drinking is the primary product. A living horse which sees a dead horse imagines its own death? Solution. If a horse did not imagine its own death, it would not have fear of death. How is visibility the product of imagination? Solution. If visibility were not imagination, the colored thing could not be imagined: therefore, visibility is thus a secondary product of imagination: just as bread is a secondary product of life. Man imagines a chimera; is that chimera a product of imagination even though it does not exist in reality? Solution. Forms/appearances which are not of true beings are instrumental, by means of which true things are genuinely apprehended. How is the imagined thing the product of imagination?
Solution. Just as the heated thing is the product of heat and the sensed thing is the product of sense, so the imagined thing is the product of imagination. Is imagining the product of imaginativeness? Solution.

*On Questions of the fruit of the Human Tree.*

What is the fruit of the human tree?
Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How is the rational soul the fruit of the body? Solution. Just as the elementary is the secondary fruit of the elements, and the elementated is the primary, so to corporify is the secondary fruit of the elementary, vegetative, sensitive, imaginative, and rational power, and it is the primary fruit according to the comparison of the fruits that are beneath it, and it is secondary according to the comparison of the rationalized, the humanified. How is man the fruit of the Sun? Solution. Just as a hammer is for a nail, and a plant is for the life of an animal, so the Sun is for man. What utility does the Sun have from the being of man? Solution. The Sun, by serving man, serves God, because man loves and knows God. Through what nature is man a nobler fruit? Solution. Man is a fruit by form, and is a fruit by end, and by form he is not the fruit of corporeal creatures, but by end he is the fruit of all corporeal creatures. What is the fruit of sinful man? Solution. That substance is empty of its fruit which is deprived of its end. And in this passage it is known how great is the punishment of the damned. In a damned man, what is the fruit of the Sun and the plant? Solution. The fruit of the Sun and the plant is lost in a damned man, inasmuch as he does not have blessedness, and restored in the judgment of God. Is Martin a better fruit of his Father than the Sun? Solution. Martin is the formal

[Column 2]

ly, finally, and materially, and is the fruit of the Sun only finally. What is Martin's meritorious fruit? Solution. Of the just is the fruit of judging, and of lovers, of loving. How are fruits alterable in men? Solution. The fruits of the craftsman who makes a nail are the coins he has for the nail, and the nail is the fruit of the man who buys it, and this from degree to degree up to living.

*On Questions of the fruit of the virtuous moral tree.*

What is the fruit of the moral tree?
Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How are moral fruits born from habits? Solution. From justice is born a just act through judging, and a good [person] made good through making good. And go to the rubric of virtue. In moral habits, how are some fruits of others? Solution. Inasmuch as one hand helps another, one hand is of the other, just as a hammer is for a nail. How are moral fruits gathered? Solution. The imaginative [faculty] gathers the colored with seeing, and words with hearing. When are moral fruits gathered? Solution. At that time, when Martin uses acts of virtues, he gathers merits. What is the fruit of hope? Solution. That merit which Martin has through hope is the fruit of hope. When Martin is despairing, where is the fruit of hope which he had? Solution. The fruit which Martin had through hope does not attain blessedness when Martin is despairing, nevertheless it attains utility, inasmuch as it is an occasion for lesser punishment. [Left Column]

Angels? Solution in the same place. How does the goodness-giving quality of God comprehend the capacity for goodness of an Angel? Solution in the same place. How is the angelic fruit full and complete? Solution in the same place. How great is the angelic fruit? Solution in the same place. Can an angel be ignorant and forget? Solution. Every creature can fail through form and matter, but by reason of its end, it cannot fail, once it has its completion in its end. From what does the fruit of an angel live? Solution. In an angel, secondary intentions live from primary ones. Is the fruit of angels from humans? Solution. The King's messenger is not from those to whom he is sent.

Concerning Questions of the fruit of the Everlasting Tree.

**F**Ruit of the everlasting tree, what are they? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Where, in what, and how are the fruits of the everlasting tree gathered? Solution in the same place. How are the fruits of goodness, greatness, duration, power, wisdom, will, virtue, truth, and glory gathered in the blessed? Solution. Go to the rubric of the fruit of goodness. Can there be any fruit in malice and from malice? Solution. Go to the rubric of the fruit of malice. Can fire torment fire, and the intellect the will? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue. Can fire afflict the soul in Hell? Solution in the same place. Will the body afflict the soul in Hell? Solution. If the soul in this life moved the body to pleasure through sin, it rightly follows that it will move it to punishment in Hell according to God's justice. If a damned man were to weep in Hell, how many tears would he shed? So-

*On Questions of the fruit of the tree of Jesus Christ.*

What is the fruit of the tree of Jesus Christ? Solution. Go to the aforesaid rubric. Who gathers the fruit of Jesus Christ? Solution, there. What utility follows from the fruit of Jesus Christ? On Questions of Species.
VIII.
What is species? Solution. Real and natural species is that subject in which genus uses difference, communicating itself to several common differing parts, which are of its essence. What is intentional species? Solution. Intentional species is that likeness which the intellect receives from real species. Where are species? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. If species were not a real being, what inconvenience would follow? Solution in the same place.

On Questions of Intensity.
IX.
What is intensity? Solution. Intensity is that figure which more strongly signifies a simple part than any other figure. Where is general and special intensity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. How does the intellect consider intensity? Solution. The intellect considers intensity by stripping the species, which it receives from common likeness, considering simple unity. Is intensity sensible? Solution. Intensity communicates itself to the sense and to the common subject, from which the sense draws it from a simple figure.

On Questions of Extensity.
X.
What is extensity? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Of what is extensity? Solution in the same place. Of what is spiritual extensity? Solution. The extension of real angelic goodness

[Right Column]

is from its real concretes, through which it is extended, and is from the likenesses which it gives to magnitude, duration, and other substantial parts of the angel's substance. How does the will extend itself in the intellect? Solution. The will extends itself in the intellect by loving in it several different things, and the more it loves them, the more it extends its act in them.

On Questions of Abstraction.
XI.
What is abstraction? Solution. Abstraction is that first and common form to its concretes, which are of its essence, in which the intellect does not consider another commonality. And go to the aforementioned rubric. What are secondary abstractions? Solution in the same place. Abstraction is, that primary causes exist. How many species of abstraction are there? Solution. There are two, one is real, the other intentional, which, being intentional, is a real likeness. And go to the rubric, as above.

On Questions of the Concrete.
XII.
What is the concrete? Solution. The concrete is that object to which abstraction is a reason, that it may be sustained in it, and that it may be a reason of operation for itself according to its nature. What are primary concretes? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Where are primary concretes? Solution in the same place. Is there motion in primary concretes? Solution. Just as secondary concretes are in potentiality in primary ones before they exist, there is motion in potentiality in primary concretes, and it comes into act.

What is the Void? Solution. The Void is that subject in which the ends of things are not reached, through which the parts of substances have no rest. How many species of void are there? Solution. There are two species of void, which you will find in the aforementioned rubric. *Concerning Questions of lightness.*
XX.
What is lightness? Solution. Lightness is that form which causes matter to ascend upwards. Is lightness a general principle? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since the form of fire is more full than matter, why is matter not lighter than form? Solution. That part in which there is more virtue moves more quickly to its center than that in which there is less. Since fire is light materially and formally, why does it descend downwards, when descent must be by ponderousness, just as ascent is by lightness? Solution. The purpose of planets and animals attracts the virtue of celestial bodies downwards. And go to the aforementioned rubric.

*Concerning Questions of ponderousness.*
XXI.
What is ponderousness? Solution. Is ponderousness a general principle? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Since rainwater is heavy, why does it ascend upwards? Solution. Ibid. From what is ponderousness? Solution. Ponderousness is from itself inasmuch as it is a general principle, and it is from several natural appetites inasmuch as it is extended in them, so that with it they may descend to the center which they desire.

*Concerning Questions of totality.*
XXII.
What is totality? Solution. Totality is the multiplication of several things which are its parts. Is totality a general principle? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Can totality exist without a part? Solution. In creatures, totality and parts are related inasmuch as there is greaterness and lesser-ness between them; nevertheless, each part is whole in itself. And in this passage, it is understood how God is whole in Himself without a part, and has in Himself a personal relation through equality without greaterness and lesser-ness. Is created goodness whole by itself, or by another? Solution. Goodness is whole by totality, just as it is great by greatness.

*Concerning Questions of a part.*
XXIII.
What is a part? Solution. A part is that form which, with its equal form, multiplies the whole, and is subject to difference. Is a part a general principle? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Can a part exist by itself? Solution. A part can formally exist by itself; but because ultimately the whole is its center, according to its end, it cannot exist by itself; indeed, it must be sustained in its common whole, joined from several parts. Can a part which is made from the whole be a general principle? Solution. Go to the rubric of virtue.

**Question concerning a hundred forms. 657**

Can motion exist without station?
Solution. If there were no station of parts, motion would not have a subject in which it could exist.

**Concerning Questions of Hardness.**
**XXVIII.**

**W**hat is hardness? Solution. Hardness is that form which is more contrary to softness than any other form. Is hardness a general form? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is hardness? Solution. Hardness exists so that the parts of a substance can exist without their contraries within the substance, into which they cannot enter. And hardness exists by reason of the dryness of the earth and the restriction of water. Why are bones harder than flesh? Solution. Because station formally suits bones, and motion finally suits flesh.

**Concerning Questions of Softness.**
**XXIX.**

**W**hat is softness? Solution. Softness is that form which opens the gates of hardness, so that certain parts can enter into others, and so that influx and reflux may have places through which they can pass. Is softness a general form? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is molten silver soft? Solution. Just as silver which is not molten is hard because of the coldness of water, so it is soft through the heat of fire when it is molten. And in this passage it is recognized that heat, against coldness, has a concordance with softness. Why does cold water restrict a human? Solution. Just as the heat of fire has a concordance with hardness in the tile which it dries, because it has a concordance with earth through dryness, so water has a concordance with air in the stomach of a human by restricting its humidity with coldness, which has a concordance with the humidity of air. And in this passage there is much concerning medicine and the mutation of the Alchemist.

**Concerning Questions of Length.**
**XXX.**

**W**hat is length? Solution. Length is that form by reason of which multiple points constitute a line. Is length a general form? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is length? Solution. Length exists formally, because multiple points or parts participate more through contraction from high to low, and finally it exists so that there may be a line which participates with heights and infinities. From what is length? Solution. Length is from itself, inasmuch as it is a simple form, and it is a part of the body, so that through it (the body) can exist.

**Concerning Questions of Breadth.**
**XXXI.**

**W**hat is breadth? Solution. Breadth is that form by reason of which multiple parts can be collateral. Is breadth a general form? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is breadth more the cause of surface than length? Solution. Just as length is the cause of the spine through a line and through heat and dryness, so breadth is the cause of surface through the collateration of humidity and coldness. In goodness what is OOoo

cause of breadth? Solution. To make good is the cause of breadth thus through collateration, just as the one making good is through length, and the one able to be made good is through depth.

*On Questions of Depth.*

XXXII.

What is depth? Solution. Depth is the middle of breadth and length, through which there is a center in the middle of substance. Is depth a general form? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Does the depth of Saturn pass as far as Venus? Solution. If the depth of Saturn were to pass as far as Venus? Solution. If the depth of Saturn were to pass as far as Venus, the depth of the Moon would pass as far as Mars, and the Sun would not be a common center by virtue of the depth of Saturn and the Moon. Roundness is thus from several collateral and contiguous circles from top to bottom, just as a line is from several points. And in this passage it is recognized that a circle is from a surface upon length, breadth, and

**Question of a hundred forms. 659**

The species of act which is through form, is made, and that which is through end, is in becoming. Form and matter, in which of the two species of act do they have greater concordance? Solution. In natural substances, the form which is produced from potentiality into actuality, is more close to matter than the form which is in producing, and is not produced.

**On Questions of Priority.**
**XXXVI.**
What is priority? Solution. Priority is that being, by reason of which one being is before another. And go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is priority? Solution. Priority is, so that certain natures can be before others, and that there can be a succession from beginning to end. Does priority have greater concordance with forms which are in potentiality than with forms which are in actuality? Solution. Although an effect is in potentiality before it is in actuality, it is necessary that it be in the cause before it is in the effect: therefore possibilities are disposed according to habits, and forms are more noble than matters. Is priority a general form? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric.

**On Questions of Secondariness.**
**XXXVII.**
What is secondariness? Solution. Secondariness is that term, in which ultimacy begins, in which second intentions and consequences begin. How is secondariness behind priority? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. From

---
[Right column]

what is secondariness? Solution. Secondariness is from consequences and from natural novelties. Can secondariness be priority? Solution. In the succession of posteriority, which is a consequence of its antecedent, there is priority of its consequent, through which there is thirdness.

**On Questions of Thirdness.**
**XXXVIII.**
What is thirdness? Solution. Thirdness is that term in which the third number is born and the second number ends, and in which the natural end is sustained. From what is natural thirdness? Solution. Every natural end is from its beginning and middle. How is thirdness behind secondariness? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. Why is thirdness? Solution. Thirdness is, so that there may be a complement and an influx and a reflux from the end, beginning, and middle.

**On Questions of Augmentation.**
**XXXIX.**
What is augmentation? Solution. Augmentation is the act of greaterness and succession, and through which one can be from many. Is augmentation a general form? Solution. Go to the aforementioned rubric. From what is augmentation? Solution. Augmentation formally is of itself, and is composed of many. Why is augmentation? Solution. Augmentation is formally through itself, and finally is so that there may be succession and motion from beginning to end in natural substances.

Consumption is that term in
which the old augmentation is lost, and
in which a new augmentation begins.
Is Consumption a general form? So-
lution. Go to the aforesaid rubric.
Of what is Consumption? Solution. Con-
sumption formally is of itself, and fi-
nally is of the corruptions of parts.
Are Consumption and corruption one
and the same in number? Solution. Insofar as
consumption is an act of minority, and
corruption signifies the privation of minority,
they are different forms, corruption
and consumption.

Of what is Disposition? Solution.
Disposition is from possibilities pre-
